title: Batterie faible ou déchargée
content: PANNE TECHNIQUE [FAULT-BAT-001] : Batterie faible ou déchargée. Système : Démarrage / Électrique. Catégorie : Électrique. Description : La batterie ne stocke plus assez d'énergie pour alimenter le démarreur et maintenir les calculateurs au-dessus du seuil critique. Gravité : Immobilisation temporaire · Risque mécanique nul. Fourchette de coût estimée : 80€ à 200€. Danger sécuritaire : NON.
source_name: AutoDiag Diagnostic Sensory Trees & Workshop Heuristics

title: Connexion de batterie oxydée ou desserrée
content: PANNE TECHNIQUE [FAULT-BAT-002] : Connexion de batterie oxydée ou desserrée. Système : Démarrage / Électrique. Catégorie : Électrique. Description : Un dépôt blanchâtre de sulfate ou une cosse desserrée crée une résistance de contact qui bloque le fort courant nécessaire au démarrage. Gravité : Faux contact · Risque de coupure subite. Fourchette de coût estimée : 15€ à 50€. Danger sécuritaire : NON.
source_name: AutoDiag Diagnostic Sensory Trees & Workshop Heuristics

title: Démarreur ou solénoïde en défaut
content: PANNE TECHNIQUE [FAULT-STA-001] : Démarreur ou solénoïde en défaut. Système : Démarrage. Catégorie : Mécanique. Description : Le moteur électrique qui entraîne le volant moteur est bloqué, les charbons internes sont usés ou le solénoïde d'engagement ne commute plus. Gravité : Panne mécanique · Remplacement atelier recommandé. Fourchette de coût estimée : 250€ à 550€. Danger sécuritaire : NON.
source_name: AutoDiag Diagnostic Sensory Trees & Workshop Heuristics

title: Pompe à carburant ou circuit de gavage
content: PANNE TECHNIQUE [FAULT-FUE-001] : Pompe à carburant ou circuit de gavage. Système : Alimentation / Carburant. Catégorie : Mécanique. Description : Le moteur tourne normalement au démarreur mais ne s'enflamme pas par absence d'arrivée d'essence ou de gazole sous pression. Gravité : Absence d'injection · Remorquage nécessaire. Fourchette de coût estimée : 180€ à 420€. Danger sécuritaire : NON.
source_name: AutoDiag Diagnostic Sensory Trees & Workshop Heuristics

title: Bougies d'allumage ou bobines d'allumage fatiguées
content: PANNE TECHNIQUE [FAULT-IGN-001] : Bougies d'allumage ou bobines d'allumage fatiguées. Système : Allumage. Catégorie : Moteur. Description : L'étincelle est trop faible ou absente sur un cylindre, provoquant des ratés d'allumage, un ralenti bancal et des trous à l'accélération. Gravité : Ratés moteur · Risque d'endommager le catalyseur. Fourchette de coût estimée : 80€ à 220€. Danger sécuritaire : NON.
source_name: AutoDiag Diagnostic Sensory Trees & Workshop Heuristics

title: Bougies de préchauffage usées (Diesel)
content: PANNE TECHNIQUE [FAULT-GLW-001] : Bougies de préchauffage usées (Diesel). Système : Allumage / Préchauffage. Catégorie : Moteur. Description : Les bougies crayons ne montent plus à incandescence à froid, rendant le premier démarrage du matin très difficile par temps froid. Gravité : Démarrage difficile à froid · Fumée blanche au démarrage. Fourchette de coût estimée : 120€ à 280€. Danger sécuritaire : NON.
source_name: AutoDiag Diagnostic Sensory Trees & Workshop Heuristics

title: Alternateur hors service ou courroie détendue
content: PANNE TECHNIQUE [FAULT-ALT-001] : Alternateur hors service ou courroie détendue. Système : Électrique / Charge. Catégorie : Électrique. Description : L'alternateur ne génère plus les 14V nécessaires pour recharger la batterie et alimenter le véhicule moteur tournant. Gravité : Arrêt complet du véhicule en roulant sous 20 minutes. Fourchette de coût estimée : 280€ à 580€. Danger sécuritaire : NON.
source_name: AutoDiag Diagnostic Sensory Trees & Workshop Heuristics

title: Vanne EGR encrassée par la calamine
content: PANNE TECHNIQUE [FAULT-EGR-001] : Vanne EGR encrassée par la calamine. Système : Antipollution / Échappement. Catégorie : Moteur. Description : La suie des gaz d'échappement bloque la vanne en position ouverte, étouffant le moteur avec trop de gaz recyclés à l'accélération. Gravité : Perte de puissance · Fumée noire · Colmatage FAP. Fourchette de coût estimée : 150€ à 380€. Danger sécuritaire : NON.
source_name: AutoDiag Diagnostic Sensory Trees & Workshop Heuristics

title: Plaquettes de frein usées au témoin
content: PANNE TECHNIQUE [FAULT-BRK-001] : Plaquettes de frein usées au témoin. Système : Freinage. Catégorie : Sécurité. Description : La garniture de friction est presque à zéro. Le support métallique commence à frotter directement sur le disque de frein. Gravité : Sécurité vitale · Distance de freinage allongée. Fourchette de coût estimée : 90€ à 200€. Danger sécuritaire : OUI - Risque sécurité routière ou casse moteur.
source_name: AutoDiag Diagnostic Sensory Trees & Workshop Heuristics

title: Air ou eau dans le circuit de liquide de frein (Pédale molle)
content: PANNE TECHNIQUE [FAULT-BRK-002] : Air ou eau dans le circuit de liquide de frein (Pédale molle). Système : Freinage. Catégorie : Sécurité. Description : Le liquide de frein hygroscopique a absorbé de l'eau ou contient des bulles d'air compressibles, rendant la pédale spongieuse. Gravité : Danger immédiat · Risque de perte totale de freinage. Fourchette de coût estimée : 60€ à 130€. Danger sécuritaire : OUI - Risque sécurité routière ou casse moteur.
source_name: AutoDiag Diagnostic Sensory Trees & Workshop Heuristics

title: Fuite joint de culasse ou échangeur (Fumée blanche)
content: PANNE TECHNIQUE [FAULT-HGD-001] : Fuite joint de culasse ou échangeur (Fumée blanche). Système : Refroidissement / Moteur. Catégorie : Moteur. Description : Le joint de culasse ne garantit plus l'étanchéité : le liquide de refroidissement passe dans les cylindres et sort en vapeur blanche persistante. Gravité : Urgence moteur majeure · Ne pas rouler avec surchauffe. Fourchette de coût estimée : 600€ à 1500€. Danger sécuritaire : OUI - Risque sécurité routière ou casse moteur.
source_name: AutoDiag Diagnostic Sensory Trees & Workshop Heuristics

title: Thermostat (Calorstat) bloqué en position fermée
content: PANNE TECHNIQUE [FAULT-THM-001] : Thermostat (Calorstat) bloqué en position fermée. Système : Refroidissement. Catégorie : Moteur. Description : La vanne thermostatique reste bloquée fermée : le liquide surchauffé tourne en boucle dans le bloc moteur sans jamais traverser le radiateur. Gravité : Surchauffe rapide en quelques kilomètres. Fourchette de coût estimée : 90€ à 220€. Danger sécuritaire : OUI - Risque sécurité routière ou casse moteur.
source_name: AutoDiag Diagnostic Sensory Trees & Workshop Heuristics

title: Motoventilateur de radiateur ou relais de commande HS
content: PANNE TECHNIQUE [FAULT-RAD-001] : Motoventilateur de radiateur ou relais de commande HS. Système : Refroidissement. Catégorie : Électrique / Refroidissement. Description : Le ventilateur ne démarre pas à basse vitesse ou dans les bouchons pour créer le flux d'air indispensable à travers la calandre. Gravité : Surchauffe en ville et dans les embouteillages. Fourchette de coût estimée : 120€ à 290€. Danger sécuritaire : OUI - Risque sécurité routière ou casse moteur.
source_name: AutoDiag Diagnostic Sensory Trees & Workshop Heuristics

title: Roulement de roue avant ou arrière usé
content: PANNE TECHNIQUE [FAULT-WHL-001] : Roulement de roue avant ou arrière usé. Système : Châssis / Train roulant. Catégorie : Mécanique. Description : Les billes d'acier du roulement sont piquées par l'usure, créant un grondement continu sourd qui s'intensifie avec la vitesse du véhicule. Gravité : Bruit sourd · Jeu mécanique progressif dans le moyeu. Fourchette de coût estimée : 130€ à 280€. Danger sécuritaire : NON.
source_name: AutoDiag Diagnostic Sensory Trees & Workshop Heuristics

title: Courroie d'accessoires détendue ou glacée
content: PANNE TECHNIQUE [FAULT-BELT-001] : Courroie d'accessoires détendue ou glacée. Système : Moteur / Périphériques. Catégorie : Mécanique. Description : La courroie striée patine sur les poulies d'alternateur et de pompe à eau, produisant un sifflement strident aigu au démarrage à froid. Gravité : Couinement strident · Risque de rupture de courroie. Fourchette de coût estimée : 50€ à 140€. Danger sécuritaire : NON.
source_name: AutoDiag Diagnostic Sensory Trees & Workshop Heuristics

title: Fusible grillé sur la boîte de distribution
content: PANNE TECHNIQUE [FAULT-FUS-001] : Fusible grillé sur la boîte de distribution. Système : Électrique. Catégorie : Électrique. Description : Le filament de protection calibré a fondu pour préserver le faisceau lors d'une surintensité électrique. Gravité : Panne simple · Remplacement immédiat et économique. Fourchette de coût estimée : 5€ à 25€. Danger sécuritaire : NON.
source_name: AutoDiag Diagnostic Sensory Trees & Workshop Heuristics

title: Faisceau de portière ou hayon sectionné dans le soufflet
content: PANNE TECHNIQUE [FAULT-WRG-001] : Faisceau de portière ou hayon sectionné dans le soufflet. Système : Électrique / Habitacle. Catégorie : Électrique. Description : Les fils de cuivre se rompent à l'intérieur du soufflet caoutchouc à force d'ouvertures répétées de la porte. Gravité : Faux contact intermittent · Problème vitre ou verrouillage. Fourchette de coût estimée : 60€ à 180€. Danger sécuritaire : NON.
source_name: AutoDiag Diagnostic Sensory Trees & Workshop Heuristics

title: Filtre à air très encrassé ou colmaté
content: PANNE TECHNIQUE [FAULT-AIR-001] : Filtre à air très encrassé ou colmaté. Système : Admission / Moteur. Catégorie : Moteur. Description : Le moteur étouffe par manque d'air propre et compense en injectant davantage de carburant pour maintenir la vitesse. Gravité : Surconsommation de 10 à 20% · Perte de vivacité. Fourchette de coût estimée : 20€ à 55€. Danger sécuritaire : NON.
source_name: AutoDiag Diagnostic Sensory Trees & Workshop Heuristics

title: Sous-gonflage important des pneumatiques
content: PANNE TECHNIQUE [FAULT-TYR-001] : Sous-gonflage important des pneumatiques. Système : Châssis / Pneumatiques. Catégorie : Sécurité. Description : Une pression trop basse augmente la surface de contact et la résistance au roulement, forçant le moteur à consommer plus. Gravité : Surconsommation · Risque d'échauffement et d'éclatement. Fourchette de coût estimée : 0€ à 30€. Danger sécuritaire : OUI - Risque sécurité routière ou casse moteur.
source_name: AutoDiag Diagnostic Sensory Trees & Workshop Heuristics

title: Test d'effondrement des phares (sans outil)
content: TEST ET CONTRÔLE [FAULT-BAT-001 - Batterie faible ou déchargée] : Test d'effondrement des phares (sans outil). Type de test : visual. Instruction pas-à-pas : Allumez vos feux de croisement ou le plafonnier, puis essayez de tourner la clé de contact. Résultat attendu / observation : Si les phares s'éteignent net ou faiblissent comme une bougie au coup de clé, la batterie est à plat. Outils nécessaires : Aucun outil (observation visuelle immédiate). Durée estimée : 5 min. Consignes de sécurité : Ne court-circuitez pas les bornes avec des outils métalliques.
source_name: AutoDiag Diagnostic Sensory Trees & Workshop Heuristics

metadata.safety_warning: Ne court-circuitez pas les bornes avec des outils métalliques.

title: Inspection visuelle et manuelle des cosses
content: TEST ET CONTRÔLE [FAULT-BAT-002 - Connexion de batterie oxydée ou desserrée] : Inspection visuelle et manuelle des cosses. Type de test : action. Instruction pas-à-pas : Moteur coupé, essayez de faire tourner les colliers de batterie à la main. Résultat attendu / observation : Les cosses doivent être parfaitement rigides sans aucun jeu ni poudre verdâtre/blanchâtre. Outils nécessaires : Gants de protection. Durée estimée : 5 min.
source_name: AutoDiag Diagnostic Sensory Trees & Workshop Heuristics

title: Test d'écoute du claquement sec avec phares stables
content: TEST ET CONTRÔLE [FAULT-STA-001 - Démarreur ou solénoïde en défaut] : Test d'écoute du claquement sec avec phares stables. Type de test : acoustic. Instruction pas-à-pas : Baissez la vitre, allumez les phares et tournez la clé à fond. Résultat attendu / observation : Si vous entendez un "clac" sec sous le capot sans rotation moteur alors que les phares restent bien vifs, le démarreur reçoit le courant mais ne tourne pas. Outils nécessaires : Test auditif sans outil. Durée estimée : 5 min.
source_name: AutoDiag Diagnostic Sensory Trees & Workshop Heuristics

title: Test du sifflement électrique de gavage
content: TEST ET CONTRÔLE [FAULT-FUE-001 - Pompe à carburant ou circuit de gavage] : Test du sifflement électrique de gavage. Type de test : acoustic. Instruction pas-à-pas : Dans un endroit silencieux, mettez le contact (voyants allumés) sans tourner la clé jusqu'au démarrage. Résultat attendu / observation : Vous devez entendre un discret "bzzzz" électrique pendant 2 secondes venant de l'arrière du véhicule. Si silence total, la pompe ne tourne pas. Outils nécessaires : Test auditif. Durée estimée : 5 min.
source_name: AutoDiag Diagnostic Sensory Trees & Workshop Heuristics

title: Test de tremblement au ralenti
content: TEST ET CONTRÔLE [FAULT-IGN-001 - Bougies d'allumage ou bobines d'allumage fatiguées] : Test de tremblement au ralenti. Type de test : action. Instruction pas-à-pas : Moteur allumé au point mort, posez vos mains sur le volant et donnez de petites accélérations douces. Résultat attendu / observation : Des secousses rythmées ou un son de moteur qui tourne "sur 3 pattes" confirment un raté d'allumage. Outils nécessaires : Ressenti tactile. Durée estimée : 5 min.
source_name: AutoDiag Diagnostic Sensory Trees & Workshop Heuristics

title: Test du double préchauffage par temps froid
content: TEST ET CONTRÔLE [FAULT-GLW-001 - Bougies de préchauffage usées (Diesel)] : Test du double préchauffage par temps froid. Type de test : action. Instruction pas-à-pas : Mettez le contact 2 fois de suite pour laisser le voyant spirale préchauffer deux fois avant de lancer le démarreur. Résultat attendu / observation : Si le moteur démarre nettement mieux au double préchauffage, une ou plusieurs bougies de préchauffage sont coupées. Outils nécessaires : Test au tableau de bord. Durée estimée : 5 min.
source_name: AutoDiag Diagnostic Sensory Trees & Workshop Heuristics

title: Observation du voyant batterie moteur tournant
content: TEST ET CONTRÔLE [FAULT-ALT-001 - Alternateur hors service ou courroie détendue] : Observation du voyant batterie moteur tournant. Type de test : visual. Instruction pas-à-pas : Après démarrage (aux câbles si nécessaire), observez le combiné d'instruments. Résultat attendu / observation : Si le voyant batterie rouge reste allumé en roulant, l'alternateur ne recharge pas. Outils nécessaires : Observation combiné. Durée estimée : 5 min.
source_name: AutoDiag Diagnostic Sensory Trees & Workshop Heuristics

title: Test d'accélération franche sous charge
content: TEST ET CONTRÔLE [FAULT-EGR-001 - Vanne EGR encrassée par la calamine] : Test d'accélération franche sous charge. Type de test : action. Instruction pas-à-pas : En 3ème vitesse sur voie dégagée, accélérez à fond entre 2000 et 3000 tr/min. Résultat attendu / observation : Un trou d'accélération avec un nuage de fumée noire dans le rétroviseur trahit une vanne EGR grippée. Outils nécessaires : Essai dynamique. Durée estimée : 5 min.
source_name: AutoDiag Diagnostic Sensory Trees & Workshop Heuristics

title: Contrôle visuel à travers la jante et bruit au freinage
content: TEST ET CONTRÔLE [FAULT-BRK-001 - Plaquettes de frein usées au témoin] : Contrôle visuel à travers la jante et bruit au freinage. Type de test : visual. Instruction pas-à-pas : Roues braquées, éclairez l'étrier de frein à travers les branches de la jante. Résultat attendu / observation : La garniture doit mesurer au moins 3 mm. Si vous entendez un grincement métallique de ferraille en freinant, la plaquette est à la ferraille. Outils nécessaires : Lampe torche smartphone. Durée estimée : 5 min.
source_name: AutoDiag Diagnostic Sensory Trees & Workshop Heuristics

title: Test d'enfoncement prolongé de la pédale à l'arrêt
content: TEST ET CONTRÔLE [FAULT-BRK-002 - Air ou eau dans le circuit de liquide de frein (Pédale molle)] : Test d'enfoncement prolongé de la pédale à l'arrêt. Type de test : action. Instruction pas-à-pas : Moteur allumé à l'arrêt, appuyez fermement sur la pédale de frein pendant 15 secondes sans relâcher. Résultat attendu / observation : La pédale doit rester dure et fixe. Si elle descend lentement jusqu'au plancher, le circuit a une fuite ou une bulle d'air. Outils nécessaires : Test pédale sans outil. Durée estimée : 5 min.
source_name: AutoDiag Diagnostic Sensory Trees & Workshop Heuristics

title: Test du bouchon d'huile (recherche de mayonnaise)
content: TEST ET CONTRÔLE [FAULT-HGD-001 - Fuite joint de culasse ou échangeur (Fumée blanche)] : Test du bouchon d'huile (recherche de mayonnaise). Type de test : visual. Instruction pas-à-pas : Moteur froid, dévissez le bouchon de remplissage d'huile moteur et retournez-le. Résultat attendu / observation : Une émulsion beigeâtre crémeuse ("mayonnaise") sous le bouchon prouve le mélange eau/huile. Outils nécessaires : Chiffon propre. Durée estimée : 5 min.
source_name: AutoDiag Diagnostic Sensory Trees & Workshop Heuristics

title: Test thermique de la durite supérieure de radiateur
content: TEST ET CONTRÔLE [FAULT-THM-001 - Thermostat (Calorstat) bloqué en position fermée] : Test thermique de la durite supérieure de radiateur. Type de test : action. Instruction pas-à-pas : Moteur tiède (aiguille qui commence à monter), touchez prudemment la grosse durite supérieure du radiateur. Résultat attendu / observation : Si le moteur est brûlant mais que la durite et le radiateur restent complètement froids, le calorstat est bloqué fermé. Outils nécessaires : Gants de protection thermique. Durée estimée : 5 min.
source_name: AutoDiag Diagnostic Sensory Trees & Workshop Heuristics

title: Test d'enclenchement forcé via la climatisation
content: TEST ET CONTRÔLE [FAULT-RAD-001 - Motoventilateur de radiateur ou relais de commande HS] : Test d'enclenchement forcé via la climatisation. Type de test : action. Instruction pas-à-pas : Moteur tournant au ralenti à l'arrêt, activez la climatisation sur A/C MAX. Résultat attendu / observation : L'enclenchement de la clim force légalement le ventilateur de radiateur à tourner dans les 15 secondes. S'il reste inerte, son moteur ou relais est HS. Outils nécessaires : Commande habitacle. Durée estimée : 5 min.
source_name: AutoDiag Diagnostic Sensory Trees & Workshop Heuristics

title: Test de variation acoustique en appui dynamique
content: TEST ET CONTRÔLE [FAULT-WHL-001 - Roulement de roue avant ou arrière usé] : Test de variation acoustique en appui dynamique. Type de test : acoustic. Instruction pas-à-pas : Sur route dégagée à 70 km/h, effectuez de légers virages gauche/droite. Résultat attendu / observation : Si le bourdonnement sourd s'amplifie en virant d'un côté (roue en appui) et s'atténue de l'autre, le roulement chargé est usé. Outils nécessaires : Essai dynamique. Durée estimée : 5 min.
source_name: AutoDiag Diagnostic Sensory Trees & Workshop Heuristics

title: Test de la goutte d'eau sur la courroie
content: TEST ET CONTRÔLE [FAULT-BELT-001 - Courroie d'accessoires détendue ou glacée] : Test de la goutte d'eau sur la courroie. Type de test : action. Instruction pas-à-pas : Moteur froid émettant le couinement au ralenti, vaporisez quelques gouttes d'eau claire sur la courroie. Résultat attendu / observation : Si le cri aigu cesse immédiatement pendant 10 secondes avant de reprendre, la courroie est détendue ou glacée. Outils nécessaires : Un peu d'eau. Durée estimée : 5 min.
source_name: AutoDiag Diagnostic Sensory Trees & Workshop Heuristics

title: Contrôle visuel du filament de fusible
content: TEST ET CONTRÔLE [FAULT-FUS-001 - Fusible grillé sur la boîte de distribution] : Contrôle visuel du filament de fusible. Type de test : visual. Instruction pas-à-pas : Ouvrez la trappe à fusibles (habitacle ou sous capot) avec la pince plastique fournie. Résultat attendu / observation : Le cavalier plastique transparent laisse voir le filament métallique central : s'il est coupé ou noirci, le fusible est grillé. Outils nécessaires : Pince à fusibles plastique. Durée estimée : 5 min.
source_name: AutoDiag Diagnostic Sensory Trees & Workshop Heuristics

title: Test de manipulation du soufflet de portière
content: TEST ET CONTRÔLE [FAULT-WRG-001 - Faisceau de portière ou hayon sectionné dans le soufflet] : Test de manipulation du soufflet de portière. Type de test : action. Instruction pas-à-pas : Actionnez le bouton de vitre ou verrouillage tout en manipulant doucement le caoutchouc noir d'articulation de porte. Résultat attendu / observation : Si le contact se rétablit brièvement selon l'angle de la porte, un ou plusieurs fils sont coupés dans le soufflet. Outils nécessaires : Manipulation manuelle. Durée estimée : 5 min.
source_name: AutoDiag Diagnostic Sensory Trees & Workshop Heuristics

title: Contrôle visuel de l'accordéon de filtre à air
content: TEST ET CONTRÔLE [FAULT-AIR-001 - Filtre à air très encrassé ou colmaté] : Contrôle visuel de l'accordéon de filtre à air. Type de test : visual. Instruction pas-à-pas : Déclipsez le couvercle de la boîte à air sous le capot et sortez la cartouche. Résultat attendu / observation : Les plis en papier doivent être beiges ou blancs. S'ils sont noirs de suie, pleins de feuilles ou d'insectes, le filtre est étouffé. Outils nécessaires : Tournevis cruciforme ou clips. Durée estimée : 5 min.
source_name: AutoDiag Diagnostic Sensory Trees & Workshop Heuristics

title: Contrôle de pression à froid au manomètre
content: TEST ET CONTRÔLE [FAULT-TYR-001 - Sous-gonflage important des pneumatiques] : Contrôle de pression à froid au manomètre. Type de test : action. Instruction pas-à-pas : À la station de gonflage sur pneus froids, vérifiez la pression des 4 pneus selon l'étiquette de portière conducteur. Résultat attendu / observation : Si la pression mesurée est inférieure de plus de 0,5 bar à la consigne constructeur, les pneus résistent au roulement. Outils nécessaires : Manomètre de gonflage. Durée estimée : 5 min.
source_name: AutoDiag Diagnostic Sensory Trees & Workshop Heuristics

title: P0101: P0101 - Mass or Volume Air Flow Sensor A Circuit Range/Performance
content: CODE DÉFAUT OBD-II [P0101] : P0101 - Mass or Volume Air Flow Sensor A Circuit Range/Performance. Système : Powertrain (Engine & Transmission). Description technique : The mass air flow sensor (MAF) sits between the air filter and the throttle or compressor and measures how much air the engine draws in; fuel quantity, load and ignition are calculated from it. Most are hot-film or hot-wire sensors that output either a voltage or, on GM, Saab and newer Ford systems, a frequency. P0101 is a plausibility fault: the signal is electrically fine but does not match the engine's state. GM petrol engines model the expected air flow from manifold pressure, throttle, speed and boost and blame the MAF if it is off by more than 20 g/s; GM diesels check the measured-to-estimated ratio (0.8–1.2) with EGR closed; Bosch ME9 compares it with the throttle angle. Common causes are air leaks after the sensor, a soiled element (oiled sport filters) or a disconnected crankcase vent; GM also documents a bad crimp in the fuse box. Ford uses P0068 instead. Two trips are needed. Causes fréquentes : Air leak between sensor and engine (cracked or loose intake duct, boost leak) [HIGH], Contaminated sensing element (oil from oiled sport filter, dust) [HIGH], Leaking or disconnected crankcase ventilation [MEDIUM], Clogged or wrongly fitted air filter, modified intake [MEDIUM]. Urgence : Urgent / Danger. Recommandation atelier : Estimated repair: 10€ - 350€ (0.3h - 2h labor). DIY feasible with standard tools.
source_name: SAE J2012 / ISO 15031-6 Standard OBD-II Database

title: P0133: P0133 - O2 Sensor Circuit Slow Response Bank 1 Sensor 1
content: CODE DÉFAUT OBD-II [P0133] : P0133 - O2 Sensor Circuit Slow Response Bank 1 Sensor 1. Système : Powertrain (Engine & Transmission). Description technique : The oxygen sensor before the catalytic converter on bank 1 (sensor 1) is the main control sensor for the mixture. It is either a switching sensor (about 0.1 V lean to 0.9 V rich) or a wide-band sensor that works with a pump current evaluated by an interface chip. P0133 means the sensor does not react fast enough to mixture changes. Methods differ fundamentally: GM measures passively how long the signal takes to cross 400–600 mV in each direction, averaged over 60 s; Ford forces the mixture to swing at 1.5 Hz and fails a switching sensor whose amplitude stays below 0.5 V, or evaluates response times of a wide-band sensor against a no-fault area; Subaru compares controller activity with measured lambda over 210 s. The test runs once per drive at warm part load; two trips. Mixture control usually stays active, but worse. Causes fréquentes : Aged, sooted or poisoned upstream sensor (oil, silicone, coolant, additives) [HIGH], Exhaust leak ahead of the sensor (manifold gasket, crack) [MEDIUM], Sensor heater weak or intermittent (sensor too cold) [MEDIUM], Mixture fault: air leak, injectors, fuel pressure, air flow sensor [MEDIUM]. Urgence : High. Recommandation atelier : Estimated repair: 60€ - 300€ (0.5h - 1.5h labor). DIY feasible with standard tools.
source_name: SAE J2012 / ISO 15031-6 Standard OBD-II Database

title: P0171: P0171 - System Too Lean Bank 1
content: CODE DÉFAUT OBD-II [P0171] : P0171 - System Too Lean Bank 1. Système : Powertrain (Engine & Transmission). Description technique : With closed-loop control the engine module corrects the injected fuel using the oxygen sensor: short-term fuel trim reacts within fractions of a second, long-term trim stores a learned base correction per load and speed range. Positive values mean fuel is being added because the mixture was lean, negative values mean fuel is being removed; around ±10 % is normal. P0171 means long-term trim on bank 1 is at its upper limit: the module already adds the maximum fuel and the mixture still stays lean. GM sets it at a long-term factor of about 1.30–1.36 (+30–36 %, engine-specific), Ford above +25 % with short-term trim above +1 %; it needs two trips and is suspended during heavy purge flow or intrusive tests. GM bulletins repeatedly trace it to leaking crankcase ventilation hoses or pipes on V6 and V8 engines; Ford found leaking direct injectors. P0171 together with P0174 points to a shared cause. Diagnosis hint: trims very high only at idle and normal under load point to an air leak; trims rising with load point to fuel shortage or an air flow sensor reading low. The oxygen sensor only reports what is in the exhaust and is rarely the cause. Causes fréquentes : Air leak after the air flow sensor (intake manifold gasket, vacuum hoses, throttle body gasket, brake booster line) [HIGH], Crankcase ventilation leaking or faulty (PCV hose, diaphragm in valve cover, oil cap, dipstick) [HIGH], Air flow sensor dirty or drifting (measures too little air) [MEDIUM], Fuel pressure or delivery too low (weak pump, clogged filter, regulator, tank nearly empty) [MEDIUM]. Urgence : High. Recommandation atelier : Estimated repair: 20€ - 600€ (0.5h - 4h labor). DIY feasible with standard tools.
source_name: SAE J2012 / ISO 15031-6 Standard OBD-II Database

title: P0300: P0300 - Random/Multiple Cylinder Misfire Detected
content: CODE DÉFAUT OBD-II [P0300] : P0300 - Random/Multiple Cylinder Misfire Detected. Système : Powertrain (Engine & Transmission). Description technique : The engine module detects misfire from crankshaft speed: a cylinder that does not fire gives no acceleration impulse. At a catalyst-damaging rate (CARB: at least 5 % per 200 revolutions) the warning light flashes; at an emissions-relevant rate (at least 1 % per 1,000 revolutions – GM about 2–5 %, Ford 0.9–1.5 %) it comes on after two trips. Ford and GM may shut off a misfiring cylinder's injector to protect the catalyst. P0300 sets when the misfire cannot be assigned to one cylinder: several cylinders each account for more than 10 %, the cylinder changes randomly, or – at Ford – the cylinder cannot be identified at high speed. It often appears together with cylinder codes. Causes are usually systemic: false air, worn plugs on several cylinders, fuel pressure or fuel quality, valve timing – and false detection from a damaged tone wheel, rough roads or vibration. Bulletins name coils, cracked plug insulators and wrong plug gaps. Causes fréquentes : False air (vacuum leak, crankcase ventilation, intake gasket) [HIGH], Worn or wrong spark plugs on several cylinders, faulty ignition coils [HIGH], Fuel pressure too low or high, contaminated fuel [MEDIUM], Valve timing (stretched chain), valves, compression on several cylinders [LOW]. Urgence : Urgent / Danger. Recommandation atelier : Estimated repair: 30€ - 1500€ (0.5h - 6h labor). DIY feasible with standard tools.
source_name: SAE J2012 / ISO 15031-6 Standard OBD-II Database

title: P0301: P0301 - Cylinder 1 Misfire Detected
content: CODE DÉFAUT OBD-II [P0301] : P0301 - Cylinder 1 Misfire Detected. Système : Powertrain (Engine & Transmission). Description technique : The engine module detects misfire from crankshaft speed: a cylinder that does not fire gives no acceleration impulse. At a catalyst-damaging rate (CARB: at least 5 % per 200 revolutions) the warning light flashes; at an emissions-relevant rate (at least 1 % per 1,000 revolutions – GM about 2–5 %, Ford 0.9–1.5 %) it comes on after two trips. Ford and GM may shut off a misfiring cylinder's injector to protect the catalyst. P0301 means more than 90 % of the detected misfires fall on cylinder 1. Usual causes are the ignition coil or spark plug of that cylinder, its injector, or low compression; a quick test is to swap coil or plug with a neighbouring cylinder and see whether the misfire moves. Bulletins for four-cylinder engines name internal coil faults (Mazda) and plugs cracked during installation (FCA). Causes fréquentes : Ignition coil of cylinder 1 faulty (coil, connector, ground) [HIGH], Spark plug of cylinder 1 worn, sooted, cracked or wrongly gapped [HIGH], Injector of cylinder 1 clogged or leaking, or its control [MEDIUM], Low compression on cylinder 1 (valve, rings, head gasket) or local false air [LOW]. Urgence : Urgent / Danger. Recommandation atelier : Estimated repair: 30€ - 800€ (0.3h - 4h labor). DIY feasible with standard tools.

title: P0401: P0401 - EGR A Flow Insufficient Detected
content: CODE DÉFAUT OBD-II [P0401] : P0401 - EGR A Flow Insufficient Detected. Système : Powertrain (Engine & Transmission). Description technique : Exhaust gas recirculation (EGR) routes part of the exhaust back into the intake to lower combustion temperature and NOx. P0401 means too little exhaust is recirculated. Petrol engines open the valve briefly and expect a rise in manifold pressure (GM 2004 V6, MIL on the first trip); older Ford systems measure the pressure drop across an orifice (DPFE sensor). Diesels balance the air mass: if the meter sees more fresh air than the target EGR rate allows, too little exhaust flows (GM, Ford, Saab, usually MIL after two trips). Diesel causes are mostly a coked valve or cooler, petrol causes blocked passages. Causes fréquentes : EGR passages, valve or cooler carboned up [HIGH], EGR valve faulty or stuck closed [HIGH], Ford: DPFE sensor or its hoses blocked, cracked or swapped [MEDIUM], Diesel: air mass meter drifting or air leak after the turbo [MEDIUM]. Urgence : Urgent / Danger. Recommandation atelier : Estimated repair: 100€ - 900€ (1h - 4h labor). DIY feasible with standard tools.
source_name: SAE J2012 / ISO 15031-6 Standard OBD-II Database

title: P0420: P0420 - Catalyst System Efficiency Below Threshold Bank 1
content: CODE DÉFAUT OBD-II [P0420] : P0420 - Catalyst System Efficiency Below Threshold Bank 1. Système : Powertrain (Engine & Transmission). Description technique : The engine module checks whether the catalyst of bank 1 still converts enough. On petrol engines it estimates the oxygen storage capacity by comparing the sensors before and after the catalyst – a good catalyst smooths the rear signal. GM uses a test on overrun (ratio below 0.35 sets the code on the first trip), Ford an index ratio above 0.75 or fuel integration after fuel cut-off. On diesels P0420 concerns the oxidation catalyst, checked by its heat release during filter regeneration (GM Duramax LML, Ford below 45 % of the expected heat). Ford names oil-borne poisoning as the most common cause. Causes fréquentes : Catalyst aged or poisoned (oil consumption, silicone, coolant) [HIGH], Catalyst overheated by misfire or rich running [MEDIUM], Rear oxygen sensor sluggish, dirty or unsuitable [MEDIUM], Exhaust leak ahead of or at the rear sensor [MEDIUM]. Urgence : High. Recommandation atelier : Estimated repair: 80€ - 1800€ (0.5h - 3h labor). DIY feasible with standard tools.
source_name: SAE J2012 / ISO 15031-6 Standard OBD-II Database

title: P0562: P0562 - System Voltage Low
content: CODE DÉFAUT OBD-II [P0562] : P0562 - System Voltage Low. Système : Powertrain (Engine & Transmission). Description technique : The module measures its own supply voltage. CARB allows other monitors to be suspended below 11 V, and above a maker's threshold only if the voltage itself is diagnosed – that is what these codes record. GM's engine modules and Ford's PCM set them without warning lamp. P0562 means the voltage is below its threshold with the engine running, when the charging system should deliver: GM 9 V or less at 400 rpm or more in 400 of 500 samples (about 5 s), type C. Saab's 9-4X modules may switch off temporarily below about 9 V. Many other modules, such as GM's brake module, set P0562 themselves. Causes fréquentes : Alternator or regulator delivering too little [HIGH], Battery faulty (shorted cell) [HIGH], Corroded terminals, ground straps or alternator cable [MEDIUM], High quiescent current or many consumers at idle [LOW]. Urgence : Moderate. Recommandation atelier : Estimated repair: 0€ - 600€ (0.3h - 2h labor). DIY feasible with standard tools.
source_name: SAE J2012 / ISO 15031-6 Standard OBD-II Database

title: P0700: P0700 - Transmission Control System (MIL Request)
content: CODE DÉFAUT OBD-II [P0700] : P0700 - Transmission Control System (MIL Request). Système : Powertrain (Engine & Transmission). Description technique : P0700 is a notice code: the separate transmission control module has stored an emission-related fault of its own and asks the engine module to switch on the check engine light. The actual fault – a sensor, solenoid, ratio or speed sensor code – is stored in the transmission module and must be read with a tool that can address it; simple OBD readers often show only P0700. GM's engine module reads the request message from 3 s after start; Subaru-based systems (Saab 9-2X) light the MIL at once and clear it after three fault-free cycles. Ford's engine modules with integrated transmission control do not use P0700. Any limp mode comes from the transmission fault, not from P0700. Causes fréquentes : Actual fault stored in the transmission module (sensor, solenoid, ratio, speed sensor) [HIGH], Wrong transmission fluid level or condition causing slip or ratio codes [MEDIUM], Harness or connector at the transmission corroded or damaged [MEDIUM], Low system voltage or weak battery [LOW]. Urgence : High. Recommandation atelier : Estimated repair: 50€ - 1500€ (0.5h - 6h labor). Professional workshop recommended.
source_name: SAE J2012 / ISO 15031-6 Standard OBD-II Database

title: U0100: U0100 - Lost Communication with ECM/PCM "A"
content: CODE DÉFAUT OBD-II [U0100] : U0100 - Lost Communication with ECM/PCM "A". Système : Network (CAN Bus, ECU Communication). Description technique : The ECM/PCM "A" has stopped transmitting on the vehicle data bus, so other control units no longer receive its messages. As this is the engine controller itself, the engine usually will not start or run while the message is missing. Typical causes are loss of power or ground at the module, an open or shorted CAN/LIN bus wire, a connector fault, or an internal module failure. title: P0001: P0001 - Fuel Volume Regulator A Control Circuit/Open
content: CODE DÉFAUT OBD-II [P0001] : P0001 - Fuel Volume Regulator A Control Circuit/Open. Système : Powertrain (Engine & Transmission). Description technique : The fuel volume regulator (also called metering unit or suction control valve) is a solenoid valve on the inlet side of the high-pressure pump, used mainly on common-rail diesel engines. The engine control module pulses it to set how much fuel the pump draws in and delivers to the rail, and in this way controls rail pressure. P0001 is set when the control module detects that the control circuit of this valve is open, i.e. no plausible current flows when the valve is driven. Rail pressure can then no longer be controlled as intended. Whether the valve is open or closed without current depends on the design, so the same fault can cause excess pressure in one system and no pressure in another. Causes fréquentes : Connector at the regulator loose, corroded or unplugged [HIGH], Solenoid coil of the regulator open [MEDIUM], Broken wire in the harness, e.g. chafing or rodent damage [MEDIUM], Output driver in the engine control module faulty [LOW]. Urgence : Urgent / Danger. Recommandation atelier : Estimated repair: 80€ - 2500€ (0.5h - 3h labor). DIY feasible with standard tools.

title: P0005: P0005 - Fuel Shutoff Valve A Control Circuit/Open
content: CODE DÉFAUT OBD-II [P0005] : P0005 - Fuel Shutoff Valve A Control Circuit/Open. Système : Powertrain (Engine & Transmission). Description technique : The fuel shutoff valve is a solenoid valve that opens or blocks the fuel supply. On diesel engines it is usually closed without current, so that the engine stops reliably when switched off. The engine control module energises it to let fuel flow and monitors its control circuit continuously. P0005 is set when this control circuit is open. A normally closed valve then cannot open, so the engine does not start or cuts out while driving. Which vehicles use this valve and code varies by manufacturer. Causes fréquentes : Wire or connector interrupted or corroded [HIGH], Valve coil open [MEDIUM], Fuse or relay in the valve supply faulty [MEDIUM], Output driver in the engine control module faulty [LOW]. title: P0008: P0008 - Engine Position System Performance Bank 1
content: CODE DÉFAUT OBD-II [P0008] : P0008 - Engine Position System Performance Bank 1. Système : Powertrain (Engine & Transmission). Description technique : The engine control module learns how far each camshaft of bank 1 is offset from the crankshaft and compares this with a reference. P0008 is set when both camshafts of this bank are shifted in the same direction beyond a threshold. That points to the drive shared by the bank: a stretched primary timing chain, a worn tensioner, an idler gear or a crankshaft reluctor wheel that has slipped. A single faulty camshaft phaser does not set this code, because it affects only one camshaft. Causes fréquentes : Primary or timing chain stretched [HIGH], Chain tensioner worn or loose [MEDIUM], Timing drive fitted incorrectly after an engine repair [MEDIUM], Crankshaft reluctor wheel slipped [LOW]. Urgence : High. Recommandation atelier : Estimated repair: 1500€ - 4000€ (8h - 20h labor). Professional workshop recommended.

title: P000A: P000A - A Camshaft Position Slow Response Bank 1
content: CODE DÉFAUT OBD-II [P000A] : P000A - A Camshaft Position Slow Response Bank 1. Système : Powertrain (Engine & Transmission). Description technique : This monitor does not judge the end position of the intake camshaft on bank 1 but how fast it follows a change of the commanded angle. The code is set when the actual angle lags behind the target for too long during several adjustments. The adjustment speed depends directly on oil flow, so worn or wrong oil and a partly clogged screen are the usual causes. Drivability is often hardly affected; the fault is an early warning before the camshaft misses its target position altogether. Bank 1 is the cylinder bank that contains cylinder 1. Causes fréquentes : Oil too thick or too thin, sludged, or oil level low [HIGH], Screen at the oil control valve partly clogged [HIGH], Oil control valve sluggish [MEDIUM], Cam phaser leaking internally or worn [MEDIUM]. Urgence : High. Recommandation atelier : Estimated repair: 60€ - 1500€ (0.5h - 8h labor). DIY feasible with standard tools.

title: P000E: P000E - Fuel Volume Regulator Control Exceeded Learning Limit
content: CODE DÉFAUT OBD-II [P000E] : P000E - Fuel Volume Regulator Control Exceeded Learning Limit. Système : Powertrain (Engine & Transmission). Description technique : The fuel volume regulator (also called metering unit or suction control valve) is a solenoid valve on the inlet side of the high-pressure pump, used mainly on common-rail diesel engines. The engine control module pulses it to set how much fuel the pump draws in and delivers to the rail, and in this way controls rail pressure. To compensate for tolerances and wear, the control module learns a long-term correction of the regulator control. P000E is set when this correction leaves its calibrated range. The regulator is electrically fine, but the system needs an unusually large correction all the time, which points to wear or contamination of regulator or pump, a weak low-pressure supply, or a missing calibration after a pump replacement. Causes fréquentes : Fuel volume regulator worn or contaminated [HIGH], High-pressure pump worn, delivering less [MEDIUM], Low-pressure side: clogged filter, weak lift pump or air in the fuel [MEDIUM], Not calibrated after pump or regulator replacement [MEDIUM]. Urgence : Urgent / Danger. Recommandation atelier : Estimated repair: 100€ - 3000€ (1h - 4h labor). Professional workshop recommended.

title: P000F: P000F - Fuel System Over Pressure Relief Valve Activated
content: CODE DÉFAUT OBD-II [P000F] : P000F - Fuel System Over Pressure Relief Valve Activated. Système : Powertrain (Engine & Transmission). Description technique : On common-rail diesel and some gasoline direct-injection systems a spring-loaded pressure relief valve protects the rail and injectors: if pressure rises too far, it opens and returns fuel to the tank, often holding a reduced pressure for limp-home operation. The control module recognises the opening from the rail pressure signal and stores P000F. The code reports an event, not a defect of the relief valve itself; the actual cause usually lies in pressure control, for example a regulator that delivers too much fuel. Causes fréquentes : Fuel volume regulator stuck open or without current, pump over-delivers [HIGH], Rail pressure sensor reading wrong, control runs into overpressure [MEDIUM], Pressure control valve faulty, where fitted [MEDIUM], Fuel return line blocked or kinked [LOW]. Urgence : Urgent / Danger. Recommandation atelier : Estimated repair: 150€ - 2500€ (1h - 4h labor). Professional workshop recommended.

title: P0010: P0010 - "A" Camshaft Position Actuator Circuit (Bank 1)
content: CODE DÉFAUT OBD-II [P0010] : P0010 - "A" Camshaft Position Actuator Circuit (Bank 1). Système : Powertrain (Engine & Transmission). Description technique : The engine control module drives the oil control valve (a pulse-width modulated solenoid) of the variable valve timing on the intake camshaft on bank 1. It checks the electrical state of this output and sets the code when the circuit is open, or when the measured state does not match the command, for example because of a short. Camshaft adjustment is then disabled and the phaser stays in its locked rest position: the engine keeps running, but with less torque and higher consumption. Bank 1 is the cylinder bank that contains cylinder 1. Causes fréquentes : Solenoid coil of the oil control valve open or shorted [HIGH], Connector corroded, loose or soaked with engine oil wicking through the valve [HIGH], Wiring harness chafed through or broken [MEDIUM], Supply voltage missing, e.g. blown fuse [MEDIUM]. Urgence : Urgent / Danger. Recommandation atelier : Estimated repair: 50€ - 300€ (0.3h - 2h labor). DIY feasible with standard tools.

title: P0011: P0011 - "A" Camshaft Position - Timing Over-Advanced or System Performance (Bank 1)
content: CODE DÉFAUT OBD-II [P0011] : P0011 - "A" Camshaft Position - Timing Over-Advanced or System Performance (Bank 1). Système : Powertrain (Engine & Transmission). Description technique : The engine control module compares the commanded position of the intake camshaft on bank 1 with the actual position it calculates from the camshaft and crankshaft sensors. This code is set when the camshaft sits further advanced than commanded for longer than a calibrated time, or, depending on the manufacturer, when the target is missed in either direction ("system performance"). Typical cause is a phaser that does not return to its rest position, for example because the oil control valve sticks open or its screen is clogged. Bank 1 is the cylinder bank that contains cylinder 1. Causes fréquentes : Oil level too low, oil sludged or wrong viscosity [HIGH], Screen at the oil control valve clogged with debris [HIGH], Oil control valve mechanically sticking [HIGH], Cam phaser worn or its locking pin sticking [MEDIUM]. Urgence : Urgent / Danger. Recommandation atelier : Estimated repair: 60€ - 1800€ (0.5h - 8h labor). DIY feasible with standard tools.

title: P0016: P0016 - Crankshaft Position - Camshaft Position Correlation (Bank 1 Sensor A)
content: CODE DÉFAUT OBD-II [P0016] : P0016 - Crankshaft Position - Camshaft Position Correlation (Bank 1 Sensor A). Système : Powertrain (Engine & Transmission). Description technique : The engine control module checks whether the signal of the intake camshaft on bank 1 (sensor A) arrives at the expected crankshaft position, usually while the camshaft phaser is in its rest position. P0016 is set when the deviation stays outside a calibrated window. title: P001A: P001A - A Camshaft Profile Actuator A Control Circuit/Open Bank 1
content: CODE DÉFAUT OBD-II [P001A] : P001A - A Camshaft Profile Actuator A Control Circuit/Open Bank 1. Système : Powertrain (Engine & Transmission). Description technique : A camshaft profile actuator switches the intake camshaft (camshaft A) on bank 1 between two or more fixed cam profiles with different valve lift and duration, for example by shifting a cam piece axially or by locking rocker arms or tappets with oil pressure. Unlike a camshaft phaser it does not shift the timing continuously. The second letter "A" in the title numbers the actuator on this camshaft. This code is set when the control circuit of the actuator is open: no current flows when it is driven, because of a broken wire, an unplugged connector or an open coil. The engine usually stays on one profile, typically the base profile with low lift. Some manufacturers report these faults with their own codes instead. Causes fréquentes : Connector at the actuator corroded, oil-soaked or loose [HIGH], Wire broken, e.g. at the valve cover [MEDIUM], Actuator coil open [MEDIUM], Output driver in the engine control module faulty [LOW]. Urgence : Urgent / Danger. Recommandation atelier : Estimated repair: 50€ - 500€ (0.5h - 2.5h labor). DIY feasible with standard tools.

title: P0020: P0020 - "A" Camshaft Position Actuator Circuit (Bank 2)
content: CODE DÉFAUT OBD-II [P0020] : P0020 - "A" Camshaft Position Actuator Circuit (Bank 2). Système : Powertrain (Engine & Transmission). Description technique : The engine control module drives the oil control valve (a pulse-width modulated solenoid) of the variable valve timing on the intake camshaft on bank 2. It checks the electrical state of this output and sets the code when the circuit is open, or when the measured state does not match the command, for example because of a short. Camshaft adjustment is then disabled and the phaser stays in its locked rest position: the engine keeps running, but with less torque and higher consumption. Bank 2 exists only on V and boxer engines; it is the cylinder bank without cylinder 1. Causes fréquentes : Solenoid coil of the oil control valve open or shorted [HIGH], Connector corroded, loose or soaked with engine oil wicking through the valve [HIGH], Wiring harness chafed through or broken [MEDIUM], Supply voltage missing, e.g. blown fuse [MEDIUM]. Urgence : Urgent / Danger. Recommandation atelier : Estimated repair: 50€ - 300€ (0.3h - 2h labor). DIY feasible with standard tools.
source_name: SAE J2012 / ISO 15031-6 Standard OBD-II Database

title: P0021: P0021 - "A" Camshaft Position - Timing Over-Advanced or System Performance (Bank 2)
content: CODE DÉFAUT OBD-II [P0021] : P0021 - "A" Camshaft Position - Timing Over-Advanced or System Performance (Bank 2). Système : Powertrain (Engine & Transmission). Description technique : The engine control module compares the commanded position of the intake camshaft on bank 2 with the actual position it calculates from the camshaft and crankshaft sensors. This code is set when the camshaft sits further advanced than commanded for longer than a calibrated time, or, depending on the manufacturer, when the target is missed in either direction ("system performance"). Typical cause is a phaser that does not return to its rest position, for example because the oil control valve sticks open or its screen is clogged. Bank 2 exists only on V and boxer engines; it is the cylinder bank without cylinder 1. Causes fréquentes : Oil level too low, oil sludged or wrong viscosity [HIGH], Screen at the oil control valve clogged with debris [HIGH], Oil control valve mechanically sticking [HIGH], Cam phaser worn or its locking pin sticking [MEDIUM]. Urgence : Urgent / Danger. Recommandation atelier : Estimated repair: 60€ - 1800€ (0.5h - 8h labor). DIY feasible with standard tools.

title: P0026: P0026 - Intake Valve Control Solenoid Circuit Range/Performance (Bank 1)
content: CODE DÉFAUT OBD-II [P0026] : P0026 - Intake Valve Control Solenoid Circuit Range/Performance (Bank 1). Système : Powertrain (Engine & Transmission). Description technique : A solenoid valve routes engine oil to a valve control element on the intake side of bank 1. Depending on the manufacturer this is a valve lift changeover or a camshaft phaser. P0026 is a plausibility fault: the electrical control is in order, but the expected effect does not occur or comes too late. The control module recognises this from feedback such as an oil pressure switch or the camshaft sensor. Pure circuit faults of the same solenoid have their own codes. The engine usually remains drivable, but with less power and higher consumption. Causes fréquentes : Oil level too low, wrong viscosity or sludged oil [HIGH], Feedback oil pressure switch faulty or leaking (systems with switch) [HIGH], Screen in front of the solenoid clogged, or solenoid sticking [MEDIUM], Mechanical fault in the valve train, e.g. locking pin or phaser sticking [MEDIUM]. Urgence : High. Recommandation atelier : Estimated repair: 50€ - 2500€ (0.5h - 12h labor). DIY feasible with standard tools.

content: CODE DÉFAUT OBD-II [P0029] : P0029 - Exhaust Valve Control Solenoid Circuit Range/Performance (Bank 2). Système : Powertrain (Engine & Transmission). Description technique : A solenoid valve routes engine oil to a valve control element on the exhaust side of bank 2. Depending on the manufacturer this is a valve lift changeover or a camshaft phaser. P0029 is a plausibility fault: the electrical control is in order, but the expected effect does not occur or comes too late. The control module recognises this from feedback such as an oil pressure switch or the camshaft sensor. Pure circuit faults of the same solenoid have their own codes. The engine usually remains drivable, but with less power and higher consumption. Bank 2 exists only on V and boxer engines. Causes fréquentes : Oil level too low, wrong viscosity or sludged oil [HIGH], Feedback oil pressure switch faulty or leaking (systems with switch) [HIGH], Screen in front of the solenoid clogged, or solenoid sticking [MEDIUM], Mechanical fault in the valve train, e.g. locking pin or phaser sticking [MEDIUM]. title: P002A: P002A - B Camshaft Profile Actuator A Control Circuit/Open Bank 1
content: CODE DÉFAUT OBD-II [P002A] : P002A - B Camshaft Profile Actuator A Control Circuit/Open Bank 1. Système : Powertrain (Engine & Transmission). Description technique : A camshaft profile actuator switches the exhaust camshaft (camshaft B) on bank 1 between two or more fixed cam profiles with different valve lift and duration, for example by shifting a cam piece axially or by locking rocker arms or tappets with oil pressure. Unlike a camshaft phaser it does not shift the timing continuously. The second letter "A" in the title numbers the actuator on this camshaft. This code is set when the control circuit of the actuator is open: no current flows when it is driven, because of a broken wire, an unplugged connector or an open coil. The engine usually stays on one profile, typically the base profile with low lift. Some manufacturers report these faults with their own codes instead. Causes fréquentes : Connector at the actuator corroded, oil-soaked or loose [HIGH], Wire broken, e.g. at the valve cover [MEDIUM], Actuator coil open [MEDIUM], Output driver in the engine control module faulty [LOW]. Urgence : Urgent / Danger. Recommandation atelier : Estimated repair: 50€ - 500€ (0.5h - 2.5h labor). DIY feasible with standard tools.

title: P0030: P0030 - HO2S Heater Control Circuit (Bank 1 Sensor 1)
content: CODE DÉFAUT OBD-II [P0030] : P0030 - HO2S Heater Control Circuit (Bank 1 Sensor 1). Système : Powertrain (Engine & Transmission). Description technique : The upstream oxygen sensor on bank 1 (sensor 1, before the catalytic converter) only delivers a usable signal once its ceramic element is hot. A heating element inside the sensor gets it there quickly after a cold start. Typically the heater receives battery voltage via a fuse or relay, and the engine control module switches the ground side with a pulsed signal while comparing the commanded state with the measured voltage or current. P0030 is the general circuit fault: the measured state does not fit the command, most often because the circuit is interrupted. Which physical fault sets P0030, P0031 or P0032 is defined by each manufacturer. Without heating, closed-loop mixture control starts late and cold-start emissions rise. Causes fréquentes : Heater circuit interrupted, e.g. broken or chafed wire near the exhaust [HIGH], Heating element inside the sensor burnt out [HIGH], Connector corroded or terminal pushed back [MEDIUM], Heater supply fuse or relay faulty [MEDIUM]. Urgence : High. Recommandation atelier : Estimated repair: 80€ - 350€ (0.5h - 1.5h labor). DIY feasible with standard tools.
source_name: SAE J2012 / ISO 15031-6 Standard OBD-II Database

title: P0033: P0033 - Turbocharger/Supercharger Bypass Valve A Control Circuit
content: CODE DÉFAUT OBD-II [P0033] : P0033 - Turbocharger/Supercharger Bypass Valve A Control Circuit. Système : Powertrain (Engine & Transmission). Description technique : The turbocharger bypass valve A is the compressor recirculation (diverter) valve: it connects the pressure side of the compressor with the intake side upstream of the turbocharger. It opens when the throttle closes quickly at high boost, so the compressor does not surge and the compressor wheel keeps its speed for the next acceleration. It is not the wastegate, which bypasses exhaust gas around the turbine and has its own codes. The valve is either electric or a vacuum unit controlled by a solenoid. P0033 is the general circuit fault, usually an open circuit: the voltage at the control output does not match the command. Causes fréquentes : Wire or connector interrupted, corroded or chafed [HIGH], Solenoid coil or electric bypass valve faulty [HIGH], Supply missing, e.g. fuse or main relay [MEDIUM], Output driver in the engine control module faulty [LOW]. Urgence : High. Recommandation atelier : Estimated repair: 50€ - 350€ (0.5h - 2h labor). DIY feasible with standard tools.

content: CODE DÉFAUT OBD-II [P0036] : P0036 - HO2S Heater Control Circuit (Bank 1 Sensor 2). Système : Powertrain (Engine & Transmission). title: P003A: P003A - Turbocharger/Supercharger Boost Control A Position Exceeded Learning Limit
content: CODE DÉFAUT OBD-II [P003A] : P003A - Turbocharger/Supercharger Boost Control A Position Exceeded Learning Limit. Système : Powertrain (Engine & Transmission). Description technique : The electric boost actuator A positions the variable turbine vanes or the wastegate and reports its position through a sensor. In a learning run, for example with the engine warm at idle or after switching off, the control module drives the actuator to its mechanical end stops and stores the sensor values as reference. P003A is set when a learned end position or the total travel lies outside the permitted limits. Typical reasons are worn or sticking vanes or linkage, a faulty actuator, a broken actuator lever, or a replacement actuator that has not been learned in. A usually denotes the first turbocharger in the exhaust flow. Causes fréquentes : Electronic actuator or its control module faulty [HIGH], Vane mechanism, sector gear or linkage worn or sticking [MEDIUM], Replacement not learned in, or learning run aborted (e.g. low voltage) [MEDIUM], Actuator lever broken [LOW]. Urgence : Urgent / Danger. Recommandation atelier : Estimated repair: 400€ - 3500€ (1h - 3h labor). Professional workshop recommended.

content: CODE DÉFAUT OBD-II [P003C] : P003C - A Camshaft Profile Actuator A Control Performance/Stuck Off Bank 1. Système : Powertrain (Engine & Transmission). Description technique : The camshaft profile actuator A switches the intake camshaft (camshaft A) on bank 1 between fixed cam profiles, usually a low-lift base profile and a high-lift profile. In most designs the unactuated state ("off") is the base profile; which profile counts as "on" is defined by the manufacturer. The control module does not need a position sensor to check the switchover: it detects the actual profile indirectly, for example from oil pressure in the switching gallery, intake pressure per cylinder or crankshaft speed fluctuations. This code is set when the switchover is commanded but the camshaft stays on the base profile, or switches too slowly or incompletely. The engine then lacks power at higher engine speed. Causes fréquentes : Oil level too low, wrong viscosity or sludged oil, so switching pressure is missing [HIGH], Profile switching solenoid sticking or its screen clogged [HIGH], Oil supply to the switching elements leaking or restricted, e.g. worn seals [MEDIUM], Locking pin in tappet or rocker arm, or sliding cam piece, sticking [MEDIUM]. Urgence : Urgent / Danger. Recommandation atelier : Estimated repair: 80€ - 3500€ (0.5h - 10h labor). DIY feasible with standard tools.

title: P0040: P0040 - O2 Sensor Signals Swapped Bank 1 Sensor 1/Bank 2 Sensor 1
content: CODE DÉFAUT OBD-II [P0040] : P0040 - O2 Sensor Signals Swapped Bank 1 Sensor 1/Bank 2 Sensor 1. Système : Powertrain (Engine & Transmission). Description technique : On engines with two exhaust banks, the control module checks whether the upstream oxygen sensors are assigned to the right bank. It changes the mixture on one bank only, actively or as part of normal bank-wise control, and watches which sensor responds. If the sensor that should sit on the other bank reacts, the signals are swapped. This logic is documented for the manufacturer-specific predecessor codes; the usual cause is connectors plugged in crosswise after a repair. If the swap remains, each bank is controlled by the other bank's signal, so fuel trims drift towards their limits. Causes fréquentes : Sensor connectors plugged in crosswise after a repair [HIGH], Harness routed wrongly or pins swapped in a connector [MEDIUM], Wrong harness, control module or calibration after a replacement [LOW]. Urgence : High. Recommandation atelier : Estimated repair: 0€ - 150€ (0.2h - 1h labor). DIY feasible with standard tools.

title: P0042: P0042 - HO2S Heater Control Circuit (Bank 1 Sensor 3)
content: CODE DÉFAUT OBD-II [P0042] : P0042 - HO2S Heater Control Circuit (Bank 1 Sensor 3). Système : Powertrain (Engine & Transmission). Description technique : The heated oxygen sensor on bank 1 is the third sensor further downstream, which exists only on systems with two catalyst stages. Its heating element brings it quickly to operating temperature. Typically the heater receives battery voltage via a fuse, and the engine control module switches the ground side with a pulsed signal while checking that the circuit state matches the command. P0042 is the general circuit fault: the measured state of the heater circuit does not fit the command, most often because the circuit is interrupted. Which physical fault sets the general, low or high code is defined by each manufacturer. Without heating, the sensor becomes ready late and catalyst monitoring may not complete. Causes fréquentes : Heating element inside the sensor burnt out [HIGH], Wire or connector damaged by heat or road spray [HIGH], Heater fuse blown; a shared fuse can set several heater codes [MEDIUM], Output driver or software of the engine control module [LOW]. Urgence : High. Recommandation atelier : Estimated repair: 80€ - 350€ (0.3h - 1.5h labor). DIY feasible with standard tools.

title: P0045: P0045 - Turbocharger/Supercharger Boost Control A Circuit/Open
content: CODE DÉFAUT OBD-II [P0045] : P0045 - Turbocharger/Supercharger Boost Control A Circuit/Open. Système : Powertrain (Engine & Transmission). Description technique : "Boost control A" is the electrically driven actuator the engine control module uses to set boost pressure: depending on the engine a pulse-width modulated solenoid or vacuum converter at the wastegate, the control valve of variable turbine vanes, or an electric actuator with position feedback. The letters A and B denote two separate actuators, for example on the low- and high-pressure turbocharger of a two-stage system, not the cylinder banks. This code is set when the control circuit is open: with the driver switched off no load can be measured, or the measured state does not match the command. Without control the actuator usually falls back to its rest position, which on most engines means low boost; depending on the design too much boost is also possible. Causes fréquentes : Connector at the actuator corroded or loose [HIGH], Wire broken or chafed through [HIGH], Solenoid coil in the actuator burnt out [MEDIUM], Fuse or ignition supply faulty [MEDIUM]. Urgence : Urgent / Danger. Recommandation atelier : Estimated repair: 50€ - 900€ (0.5h - 2.5h labor). DIY feasible with standard tools.

title: P0049: P0049 - Turbocharger/Supercharger A Turbine Overspeed
content: CODE DÉFAUT OBD-II [P0049] : P0049 - Turbocharger/Supercharger A Turbine Overspeed. Système : Powertrain (Engine & Transmission). Description technique : The control module has detected that turbocharger A runs above its permitted maximum speed. Engines equipped for it measure turbine speed with a dedicated sensor on the shaft; while the fault is active some systems continue with an estimated speed and reduce power. Real overspeed arises when too much exhaust energy reaches the turbine, for example because the wastegate or the turbine vanes stick closed, or because the turbocharger has to compensate for a charge-air leak or high altitude. Since a damaged turbocharger can fail completely, the cause should be found before driving on. Turbocharger B has its own code. Causes fréquentes : Wastegate or turbine vanes stuck closed, boost control fails [MEDIUM], Turbocharger speed sensor or its wiring faulty [MEDIUM], Charge-air leak forcing the turbocharger to higher speed [LOW], Engine control module or software [LOW]. Urgence : Urgent / Danger. Recommandation atelier : Estimated repair: 150€ - 4000€ (1h - 5h labor). Professional workshop recommended.

B is the second actuator, for example on the high-pressure turbocharger of a two-stage system or on the second turbocharger; it does not denote cylinder bank 2. This code is set when the circuit signal drops out briefly or jumps, as with a loose contact. Boost then fluctuates and reduced power may occur only now and then. Without control the actuator usually falls back to its rest position, which on most engines means low boost; depending on the design too much boost is also possible. Causes fréquentes : Loose contact at the actuator connector [HIGH], Wire broken internally by engine movement [HIGH], Corroded terminals [MEDIUM], Actuator itself faulty [LOW]. Urgence : Urgent / Danger. Recommandation atelier : Estimated repair: 50€ - 900€ (0.5h - 2.5h labor). DIY feasible with standard tools.

title: P0050: P0050 - HO2S Heater Control Circuit (Bank 2 Sensor 1)
content: CODE DÉFAUT OBD-II [P0050] : P0050 - HO2S Heater Control Circuit (Bank 2 Sensor 1). Système : Powertrain (Engine & Transmission). Description technique : The heated oxygen sensor on bank 2 is the upstream sensor (sensor 1, before the catalytic converter), used for mixture control. Its heating element brings it quickly to operating temperature. Typically the heater receives battery voltage via a fuse, and the engine control module switches the ground side with a pulsed signal while checking that the circuit state matches the command. P0050 is the general circuit fault: the measured state of the heater circuit does not fit the command, most often because the circuit is interrupted. Which physical fault sets the general, low or high code is defined by each manufacturer. Without heating, closed-loop mixture control starts late and cold-start emissions rise. Bank 2 codes occur only on engines with two exhaust banks (V or boxer engines). Causes fréquentes : Heating element inside the sensor burnt out [HIGH], Wire or connector damaged by heat or road spray [HIGH], Heater fuse blown; a shared fuse can set several heater codes [MEDIUM], Output driver or software of the engine control module [LOW]. Urgence : High. Recommandation atelier : Estimated repair: 80€ - 350€ (0.3h - 1.5h labor). DIY feasible with standard tools.

title: P0053: P0053 - HO2S Heater Resistance Bank 1 Sensor 1
content: CODE DÉFAUT OBD-II [P0053] : P0053 - HO2S Heater Resistance Bank 1 Sensor 1. Système : Powertrain (Engine & Transmission). Description technique : On bank 1, this monitor checks the heating element of the upstream sensor (sensor 1, before the catalytic converter) not for an open or short circuit, but for its resistance. Many systems measure it once after a genuine cold start, when coolant and intake air temperatures show that the sensor is at ambient temperature, and correct the value for temperature; some manufacturers evaluate the heater current instead. The code is set when the value lies outside the limits for this sensor type, typically because the element has aged. Since the test often runs only after a long standstill, the code may take a night to confirm or clear. Causes fréquentes : Heating element aged or partly damaged [HIGH], Contact resistance or corrosion at connector or pins [MEDIUM], Replacement sensor with a different heater type fitted [MEDIUM], Engine control module faulty [LOW]. Urgence : High. Recommandation atelier : Estimated repair: 80€ - 350€ (0.3h - 1.5h labor). DIY feasible with standard tools.

title: P005A: P005A - B Camshaft Profile Actuator A Control Performance/Stuck Off Bank 1
content: CODE DÉFAUT OBD-II [P005A] : P005A - B Camshaft Profile Actuator A Control Performance/Stuck Off Bank 1. Système : Powertrain (Engine & Transmission). Description technique : The camshaft profile actuator A switches the exhaust camshaft (camshaft B) on bank 1 between fixed cam profiles, usually a low-lift base profile and a high-lift profile. In most designs the unactuated state ("off") is the base profile; which profile counts as "on" is defined by the manufacturer. The control module does not need a position sensor to check the switchover: it detects the actual profile indirectly, for example from oil pressure in the switching gallery, intake pressure per cylinder or crankshaft speed fluctuations. This code is set when the switchover is commanded but the camshaft stays on the base profile, or switches too slowly or incompletely. The engine then lacks power at higher engine speed. Causes fréquentes : Oil level too low, wrong viscosity or sludged oil, so switching pressure is missing [HIGH], Profile switching solenoid sticking or its screen clogged [HIGH], Oil supply to the switching elements leaking or restricted, e.g. worn seals [MEDIUM], Locking pin in tappet or rocker arm, or sliding cam piece, sticking [MEDIUM]. Urgence : Urgent / Danger. Recommandation atelier : Estimated repair: 80€ - 3500€ (0.5h - 10h labor). DIY feasible with standard tools.

title: P0065: P0065 - Air Assisted Injector Control Range/Performance
content: CODE DÉFAUT OBD-II [P0065] : P0065 - Air Assisted Injector Control Range/Performance. Système : Powertrain (Engine & Transmission). Description technique : Air-assisted injectors have an air sleeve around the nozzle tip: air flowing past at high speed breaks the fuel spray into finer droplets, which improves combustion and cold starts and lowers hydrocarbon emissions. On port-injected engines this air is taken upstream of the throttle and dosed by a pulse-width modulated bypass solenoid; because it bypasses the throttle, it is part of the idle air. The system is rare and mainly found on older engines. P0065 means the control is electrically in order, but the effect is implausible. One documented method compares the idle speed controller correction with the air assistance switched on and off during stable idle; if the difference is too large, the code is set. Causes fréquentes : Air-assist solenoid sticking or dirty [HIGH], Air hoses to the injectors leaking, disconnected or blocked [HIGH], Air passages at the injectors coked [MEDIUM], Air leak distorting idle control [MEDIUM]. Urgence : High. Recommandation atelier : Estimated repair: 50€ - 300€ (1h - 2h labor). DIY feasible with standard tools.

title: P0068: P0068 - MAP/MAF - Throttle Position Correlation
content: CODE DÉFAUT OBD-II [P0068] : P0068 - MAP/MAF - Throttle Position Correlation. Système : Powertrain (Engine & Transmission). Description technique : The engine control module compares the air quantity measured by the manifold pressure and/or mass air flow sensor with the quantity the throttle position leads it to expect. P0068 is set when they do not match, typically because more air arrives than the nearly closed throttle allows, i.e. an air leak behind the throttle, or because the throttle body is dirty or a sensor reads wrong. On engines with electronic throttle this check protects throttle control, so the engine often goes into reduced power. Each sensor can be electrically fine on its own; regulations require such plausibility checks for input sensors with a code of their own. Causes fréquentes : Air leak behind the throttle: intake manifold, vacuum or MAP hoses [HIGH], Throttle body dirty [HIGH], Mass air flow or manifold pressure sensor faulty [MEDIUM], Engine control software (manufacturer updates exist) [MEDIUM]. Urgence : Urgent / Danger. Recommandation atelier : Estimated repair: 0€ - 300€ (0.5h - 1.5h labor). DIY feasible with standard tools.

title: P0069: P0069 - Manifold Absolute Pressure - Barometric Pressure Correlation
content: CODE DÉFAUT OBD-II [P0069] : P0069 - Manifold Absolute Pressure - Barometric Pressure Correlation. Système : Powertrain (Engine & Transmission). Description technique : With the ignition on and the engine stopped, the intake manifold is at ambient pressure, so the manifold pressure sensor and the barometric pressure sensor (often inside the control module) must read almost the same. P0069 is set when they differ by more than a threshold. Some systems also compare the barometric reading with a value estimated from manifold pressure at wide-open throttle while driving. Altitude and weather shift both values equally and do not cause the code. Each sensor can be electrically fine on its own; regulations require such plausibility checks for input sensors with a code of their own. Causes fréquentes : Manifold pressure sensor drifting [HIGH], MAP sensor hose blocked, kinked or leaking [HIGH], Barometric pressure sensor (often inside the control module) faulty [MEDIUM], 5 V reference or connector faulty [MEDIUM]. content: CODE DÉFAUT OBD-II [P006A] : P006A - MAP - Mass or Volume Air Flow Correlation Bank 1. Système : Powertrain (Engine & Transmission). A typical cause is an exhaust gas recirculation valve that does not close: recirculated exhaust raises manifold pressure without passing the air flow sensor. Air leaks, a leaking crankcase ventilation hose or a dirty sensor have the same effect. Each sensor can be electrically fine on its own; regulations require such plausibility checks for input sensors with a code of their own. title: P006E: P006E - Turbocharger/Supercharger Boost Control A Supply Voltage Circuit Low
content: CODE DÉFAUT OBD-II [P006E] : P006E - Turbocharger/Supercharger Boost Control A Supply Voltage Circuit Low. Système : Powertrain (Engine & Transmission). Description technique : "Boost control A" is the electrically driven actuator the engine control module uses to set boost pressure, for example a wastegate solenoid, the control valve of variable turbine vanes or an electric actuator. Some engines supply it through two driver stages in the control module: a high side that switches the supply voltage and a low side that switches ground. The low side is covered by P0045 to P0048; this code concerns the high side. P006E is set when the switched supply voltage is too low, typically because the supply wire is shorted to ground or interrupted. Without supply the actuator stays in its rest position, which on most engines means low boost and reduced power. Causes fréquentes : Supply wire shorted to ground or interrupted [HIGH], Connector at the actuator corroded or loose [MEDIUM], Internal short in the actuator [MEDIUM], High-side driver in the engine control module faulty [LOW]. Urgence : Urgent / Danger. Recommandation atelier : Estimated repair: 50€ - 900€ (0.5h - 2h labor). DIY feasible with standard tools.

title: P0070: P0070 - Ambient Air Temperature Sensor Circuit A
content: CODE DÉFAUT OBD-II [P0070] : P0070 - Ambient Air Temperature Sensor Circuit A. Système : Powertrain (Engine & Transmission). Description technique : The ambient air temperature sensor A is an NTC thermistor whose resistance falls as temperature rises. Its value is used by the climate control, the outside temperature display and the engine control module, which needs it to enable other diagnostics and to correct its maps. Depending on the vehicle the engine control module reads the sensor directly, or the instrument cluster or another module sends the value over the data bus; some vehicles have no sensor and estimate ambient temperature from intake air temperature. P0070 is the general circuit fault or an invalid signal, for example when the instrument cluster reports the value as invalid or the reading is implausibly low. Causes fréquentes : Sensor faulty (exposed to spray and stone chips at the front) [HIGH], Connector corroded or wire damaged, e.g. after front-end damage [HIGH], Instrument cluster or data transmission faulty (vehicles with bus-supplied value) [MEDIUM], Engine control module faulty [LOW]. Urgence : High. Recommandation atelier : Estimated repair: 40€ - 200€ (0.3h - 1h labor). DIY feasible with standard tools.

title: P0075: P0075 - Intake Valve Control Solenoid Circuit Bank 1
content: CODE DÉFAUT OBD-II [P0075] : P0075 - Intake Valve Control Solenoid Circuit Bank 1. Système : Powertrain (Engine & Transmission). Description technique : A solenoid valve on the cylinder head controls oil flow for the variable valve control on the intake side of bank 1. Depending on the manufacturer it drives a camshaft phaser (for example on Nissan engines) or a valve lift changeover (for example on Subaru engines). This code family reports electrical faults in its control circuit; P0075 is the general circuit fault: open circuit or short, without distinguishing between them. Some manufacturers use only this code for all electrical faults of the valve. Other manufacturers report the same valve under the "camshaft position actuator" codes instead. Valve control is then switched off or stays in its base position. Causes fréquentes : Solenoid coil open or shorted [HIGH], Wiring or connector interrupted, chafed or corroded [HIGH], Oil at the connector, e.g. from a leaking valve O-ring [MEDIUM], Output driver or supply in the engine control module faulty [LOW]. title: P007A: P007A - Charge Air Cooler Temperature Sensor Circuit Bank 1
content: CODE DÉFAUT OBD-II [P007A] : P007A - Charge Air Cooler Temperature Sensor Circuit Bank 1. Système : Powertrain (Engine & Transmission). Description technique : The charge air cooler temperature sensor (an NTC thermistor) measures the temperature of the compressed charge air at the charge air cooler, depending on the manufacturer upstream or downstream of it, and is often combined with the boost pressure sensor. The engine control module uses it for the air mass calculation, boost control, component protection and to monitor cooler efficiency. P007A is the general circuit fault of the bank 1 sensor; low and high signals have their own codes. No manufacturer description naming this exact code was found. Causes fréquentes : Connector or wiring faulty, oil in the connector from crankcase vapours [HIGH], Sensor faulty [HIGH], Ground or 5 V supply disturbed (often shared with the boost pressure sensor) [MEDIUM], Engine control module faulty [LOW]. Urgence : Urgent / Danger. Recommandation atelier : Estimated repair: 80€ - 250€ (0.3h - 1h labor). DIY feasible with standard tools.

title: P0087: P0087 - Fuel Rail/System Pressure - Too Low
content: CODE DÉFAUT OBD-II [P0087] : P0087 - Fuel Rail/System Pressure - Too Low. Système : Powertrain (Engine & Transmission). Description technique : On common-rail diesel and gasoline direct-injection engines, a high-pressure pump feeds the fuel rail, a sensor measures rail pressure, and the engine control module regulates it towards a target from its maps. P0087 is set when the actual pressure stays below the target by more than a threshold for some time. It is a system code: it does not say which component is at fault. Typical causes are a weak low-pressure supply, a worn high-pressure pump, a sticking control valve, a leak or a drifting pressure sensor; the engine usually goes into reduced power. Causes fréquentes : Low-pressure supply too weak: lift pump, clogged filter, low tank level or waxing [HIGH], High-pressure pump worn [HIGH], Pressure control or metering valve sticking [MEDIUM], High-pressure leak or excessive injector return flow [MEDIUM]. Urgence : Urgent / Danger. Recommandation atelier : Estimated repair: 50€ - 2500€ (0.5h - 4h labor). Professional workshop recommended.
source_name: SAE J2012 / ISO 15031-6 Standard OBD-II Database
