title: P0088: P0088 - Fuel Rail/System Pressure - Too High
content: CODE DÉFAUT OBD-II [P0088] : P0088 - Fuel Rail/System Pressure - Too High. Système : Powertrain (Engine & Transmission). Description technique : On common-rail diesel and gasoline direct-injection engines, a high-pressure pump feeds the fuel rail, a sensor measures rail pressure, and the engine control module regulates it towards a target from its maps. P0088 is set when the actual pressure stays above the target by more than a threshold for some time. On many gasoline systems the pump can only raise pressure, which is then reduced only by injecting. Typical causes are a sticking pressure control or metering valve, a drifting pressure sensor or, on diesels with a pressure control valve, a blocked return. Real overpressure can cause harsh combustion noise and smoke. Causes fréquentes : Pressure control or metering valve sticking [HIGH], Rail pressure sensor drifting [MEDIUM], Fuel return blocked (diesel with pressure control valve) [MEDIUM], Engine control software [LOW]. Urgence : Urgent / Danger. Recommandation atelier : Estimated repair: 50€ - 2500€ (0.5h - 4h labor). Professional workshop recommended.

title: P0089: P0089 - Fuel Pressure Regulator A Performance
content: CODE DÉFAUT OBD-II [P0089] : P0089 - Fuel Pressure Regulator A Performance. Système : Powertrain (Engine & Transmission). Description technique : On common-rail diesel and gasoline direct-injection engines, a high-pressure pump feeds the fuel rail, a sensor measures rail pressure, and the engine control module regulates it towards a target from its maps. The fuel pressure regulator A is the actuator the manufacturer designates for this: depending on the system a pressure control valve that releases fuel from the rail, or the control valve on the high-pressure pump. Some manufacturers report the pump valve under the "fuel volume regulator" codes instead. P0089 is a function check: pressure may still be plausible, but the regulator works at its limit, needs too much correction, or pressure does not follow its control signal. Typical causes are a sticking or worn regulator, a weak pump or a faulty pressure sensor. content: CODE DÉFAUT OBD-II [P008A] : P008A - Low Pressure Fuel System Pressure - Too Low. Système : Powertrain (Engine & Transmission). title: P008F: P008F - Engine Coolant Temperature/Fuel Temperature Correlation
content: CODE DÉFAUT OBD-II [P008F] : P008F - Engine Coolant Temperature/Fuel Temperature Correlation. Système : Powertrain (Engine & Transmission). Description technique : After the engine has been switched off long enough, coolant and fuel should have approached the same temperature. The engine control module compares the coolant temperature sensor with the fuel temperature sensor at the next cold start and sets P008F if they differ too much. From this alone it cannot tell which sensor is wrong, so both have to be checked. Regulations require such plausibility checks for input sensors; the exact conditions are manufacturer-specific. title: P0090: P0090 - Fuel Pressure Regulator A Control Circuit/Open
content: CODE DÉFAUT OBD-II [P0090] : P0090 - Fuel Pressure Regulator A Control Circuit/Open. Système : Powertrain (Engine & Transmission). Description technique : On common-rail diesel and gasoline direct-injection engines, a high-pressure pump feeds the fuel rail, a sensor measures rail pressure, and the engine control module regulates it towards a target from its maps. The fuel pressure regulator A is the actuator the manufacturer designates for this: depending on the system a pressure control valve that releases fuel from the rail, or the control valve on the high-pressure pump. Some manufacturers report the pump valve under the "fuel volume regulator" codes instead. P0090 is the general circuit fault, usually an open circuit: the driver voltage or current does not fit the command. Rail pressure can then no longer be controlled as intended, and the engine usually runs in reduced power. Causes fréquentes : Wire broken or connector corroded or loose [HIGH], Regulator coil faulty [HIGH], Fuse or supply voltage faulty [MEDIUM], Output driver in the engine control module faulty [LOW]. Urgence : Urgent / Danger. Recommandation atelier : Estimated repair: 80€ - 1200€ (0.5h - 2h labor). DIY feasible with standard tools.

title: P0093: P0093 - Fuel System Leak Detected - Large Leak
content: CODE DÉFAUT OBD-II [P0093] : P0093 - Fuel System Leak Detected - Large Leak. Système : Powertrain (Engine & Transmission). Description technique : A leak in the high-pressure fuel system is not measured directly but inferred from a pressure and volume balance. P0093 means the pump is already delivering at its limit and rail pressure still stays well below target. The leak can be external (line, rail) or internal (injector return, relief valve). An external leak is a fire hazard: stop the engine and inspect it. Causes fréquentes : High-pressure line or rail fitting leaking [HIGH], Injector with excessive leak-off [HIGH], Pressure relief or control valve leaking [MEDIUM], Weak pump or low-pressure supply mistaken for a leak [MEDIUM]. Urgence : Urgent / Danger. Recommandation atelier : Estimated repair: 100€ - 2500€ (1h - 6h labor). Professional workshop recommended.

title: P0094: P0094 - Fuel System Leak Detected - Small Leak
content: CODE DÉFAUT OBD-II [P0094] : P0094 - Fuel System Leak Detected - Small Leak. Système : Powertrain (Engine & Transmission). Description technique : A leak in the high-pressure fuel system is not measured directly but inferred from a pressure and volume balance. P0094 is typically detected when rail pressure drops too fast during overrun with injection cut off, or when more pump delivery than expected is needed at idle. Possible leaks are injectors with too much leak-off, fittings or relief valves; internal leakage can dilute the engine oil with fuel, so a rising oil level is a warning sign. title: P009B: P009B - Fuel Pressure Relief Control Circuit/Open
content: CODE DÉFAUT OBD-II [P009B] : P009B - Fuel Pressure Relief Control Circuit/Open. Système : Powertrain (Engine & Transmission). Description technique : The fuel pressure relief control is an electrically controlled valve on the fuel rail that the engine control module opens to reduce rail pressure deliberately, for example on overrun, on load drops or when the engine is switched off. It differs from the purely mechanical pressure relief valve, which opens passively at overpressure, and from the pressure regulator, which controls pressure continuously. Manufacturer documents show this code mainly on heavy-duty diesel engines. P009B reports an open control circuit of this valve. Rail pressure can then not be reduced as intended, and the engine may be derated. Causes fréquentes : Wire broken or connector corroded [HIGH], Valve coil faulty [MEDIUM], Output driver in the engine control module faulty [LOW]. Urgence : Urgent / Danger. Recommandation atelier : Estimated repair: 100€ - 900€ (0.5h - 4h labor). Professional workshop recommended.

content: CODE DÉFAUT OBD-II [P00A0] : P00A0 - Charge Air Cooler Temperature Sensor Circuit Bank 2. Système : Powertrain (Engine & Transmission). title: P00AF: P00AF - Turbocharger/Supercharger Boost Control A Module Performance
content: CODE DÉFAUT OBD-II [P00AF] : P00AF - Turbocharger/Supercharger Boost Control A Module Performance. Système : Powertrain (Engine & Transmission). Description technique : Boost control A here is an electronic actuator with its own electronics (a "smart" actuator), usually on the variable turbine geometry, with its own position sensor and controlled over a data bus or a pulsed signal. It checks itself and reports internal faults to the engine control module; documented examples are pattern errors, overcurrent and checksum errors. The control module cannot narrow down a fault inside the actuator further. P00AF is set when actuator A reports such an internal fault. Manufacturer bulletins recommend checking the vane mechanism for free movement and, if it moves freely, replacing only the actuator rather than the whole turbocharger. Causes fréquentes : Electronics or motor inside the actuator faulty [HIGH], Sector gear or vane mechanism sticking (soot, coking), causing overcurrent [MEDIUM], Weak supply or ground, corroded connector [MEDIUM], Software of actuator or control module [LOW]. Urgence : Urgent / Danger. Recommandation atelier : Estimated repair: 400€ - 3500€ (1.5h - 4h labor). Professional workshop recommended.

title: P00B6: P00B6 - Radiator Coolant Temperature/Engine Coolant Temperature Correlation
content: CODE DÉFAUT OBD-II [P00B6] : P00B6 - Radiator Coolant Temperature/Engine Coolant Temperature Correlation. Système : Powertrain (Engine & Transmission). Description technique : The radiator coolant temperature sensor is an NTC thermistor that measures coolant temperature on the radiator side, typically at the radiator outlet; the exact position depends on the manufacturer. Together with the engine coolant temperature sensor it gives a second measuring point, which the control module uses to diagnose the thermostat and coolant flow, for example on engines with an electrically heated map-controlled thermostat. After a long standstill (eight hours in a documented case) engine and radiator should be at the same temperature. P00B6 is set at the next start when the engine and radiator coolant temperature sensors differ by more than a threshold that may depend on intake air temperature. A detected engine block heater cancels the test. From this alone the control module cannot tell which sensor is wrong. Causes fréquentes : Radiator coolant temperature sensor drifting [HIGH], Engine coolant temperature sensor drifting [HIGH], Contact resistance at a connector [MEDIUM], Retrofitted engine preheater or auxiliary heater not detected by the system [MEDIUM]. Urgence : High. Recommandation atelier : Estimated repair: 50€ - 200€ (0.5h - 1.5h labor). DIY feasible with standard tools.

title: P00B7: P00B7 - Engine Coolant Flow Low/Performance
content: CODE DÉFAUT OBD-II [P00B7] : P00B7 - Engine Coolant Flow Low/Performance. Système : Powertrain (Engine & Transmission). Description technique : When the engine is hot, the thermostat should be open and coolant should flow through the radiator. P00B7 is set when the engine coolant temperature is very high (above about 117 to 119 °C in documented cases) while the radiator side stays much colder, so too little coolant flows through the radiator. The usual cause is a thermostat stuck closed; low coolant, air in the system, a pump that delivers too little or a blocked radiator have the same effect. If the temperature keeps rising, stop driving to avoid engine damage. Causes fréquentes : Thermostat stuck closed [HIGH], Low coolant level or air in the cooling system [HIGH], Coolant pump delivering too little (impeller, drive; known cases on some engines) [MEDIUM], Radiator or hoses blocked [MEDIUM]. Urgence : High. Recommandation atelier : Estimated repair: 100€ - 700€ (1h - 4h labor). DIY feasible with standard tools.

title: P00B8: P00B8 - MAP - Mass or Volume Air Flow Correlation Bank 2
content: CODE DÉFAUT OBD-II [P00B8] : P00B8 - MAP - Mass or Volume Air Flow Correlation Bank 2. Système : Powertrain (Engine & Transmission). Description technique : On engines with two intake paths, the control module compares the manifold pressure of bank 2 with the measured or calculated air quantity of that bank. P00B8 is set when the two do not fit together; the code does not say which value is wrong. As with its bank 1 counterpart, typical causes are an air leak, an exhaust gas recirculation valve that does not close, or a dirty or drifting sensor. Each sensor can be electrically fine on its own. No manufacturer description naming this exact code was found; the explanation follows its documented counterpart. Causes fréquentes : Air leak in the intake of bank 2 [HIGH], EGR valve dirty or sticking open [MEDIUM], Manifold pressure sensor or air flow meter dirty or drifting [MEDIUM], Wiring or connector faulty [LOW]. Urgence : High. Recommandation atelier : Estimated repair: 50€ - 400€ (0.5h - 2h labor). DIY feasible with standard tools.

title: P00B9: P00B9 - Low Pressure Fuel System Pressure - Too Low. Low Ambient Temperature
content: CODE DÉFAUT OBD-II [P00B9] : P00B9 - Low Pressure Fuel System Pressure - Too Low. Low Ambient Temperature. Système : Powertrain (Engine & Transmission). Description technique : This code reports too low a pressure in the low-pressure fuel supply between the lift pump and the high-pressure pump under the additional condition of low ambient temperature. It separates cold-related supply problems from the general case. A typical mechanism, documented for diesel engines, is wax separating from insufficiently winterised fuel at sub-zero temperatures and clogging the filter or tank strainer. No manufacturer description naming this exact code, its thresholds or the vehicles using it was found. Causes fréquentes : Wax separation from summer or insufficiently winterised diesel in frost [HIGH], Fuel filter clogged or water in the filter frozen [MEDIUM], Fuel filter heater faulty [MEDIUM], Lift pump weak [LOW]. Urgence : Urgent / Danger. Recommandation atelier : Estimated repair: 30€ - 600€ (0.5h - 1.5h labor). DIY feasible with standard tools.

title: P00BA: P00BA - Low Fuel Pressure - Forced Limited Power
content: CODE DÉFAUT OBD-II [P00BA] : P00BA - Low Fuel Pressure - Forced Limited Power. Système : Powertrain (Engine & Transmission). Description technique : "Forced limited power" is a term for a protective strategy in which the engine control module deliberately limits engine power. Regulations require the check engine light to come on within seconds when such an emissions-relevant limp-home mode is active. These codes report the reason for the limitation; usually further codes point to the actual cause. No manufacturer description naming this exact code was found. P00BA: power has been limited because fuel pressure is too low, which protects the engine and the pump against running lean or losing rail pressure. Causes fréquentes : Fuel filter clogged, suction-side leak or air in the system [HIGH], Lift pump or high-pressure pump weak [MEDIUM], Pressure regulator or relief valve leaking [MEDIUM], Tank run empty [MEDIUM]. Urgence : Urgent / Danger. Recommandation atelier : Estimated repair: 50€ - 1500€ (0.5h - 4h labor). Professional workshop recommended.

title: P00BC: P00BC - Mass or Volume Air Flow A Circuit Range/Performance - Air Flow Too Low
content: CODE DÉFAUT OBD-II [P00BC] : P00BC - Mass or Volume Air Flow A Circuit Range/Performance - Air Flow Too Low. Système : Powertrain (Engine & Transmission). Description technique : The control module compares the air mass measured by the air flow meter with the air mass it expects from a model, for example from manifold pressure, boost pressure and throttle position. These codes report the deviation with its direction: "too low" means the meter measures less air than expected, "too high" more. Regulations allow manufacturers to use one code for both directions or separate codes, as here. P00BC concerns air flow meter A. Typical causes are air entering behind the meter, a charge-air leak, a dirty meter or a restricted intake. No manufacturer description naming this exact code was found; the explanation follows its documented counterpart. Causes fréquentes : Air leak behind the meter or charge-air leak [HIGH], Air flow meter dirty [MEDIUM], Air filter or intake restricted [MEDIUM], Wiring or connector faulty [LOW]. Urgence : Urgent / Danger. Recommandation atelier : Estimated repair: 0€ - 350€ (0.3h - 1.5h labor). DIY feasible with standard tools.

title: P00C0: P00C0 - Turbocharger/Supercharger Bypass Valve B Control Circuit
content: CODE DÉFAUT OBD-II [P00C0] : P00C0 - Turbocharger/Supercharger Bypass Valve B Control Circuit. Système : Powertrain (Engine & Transmission). Description technique : Bypass valve B is the compressor recirculation (diverter) valve of turbocharger B, not the wastegate: it lets charge air flow back to the compressor inlet when the throttle closes quickly, so the compressor does not surge. Turbocharger B is the second turbocharger in exhaust flow on series systems and the turbocharger of bank 2 on parallel twin-turbo engines. P00C0 is the general circuit fault, usually an open circuit in the control circuit of this valve; the circuit is monitored continuously. Causes fréquentes : Wiring or connector damaged by turbocharger heat [HIGH], Valve coil open or shorted [MEDIUM], Output driver in the engine control module faulty [LOW]. Urgence : High. Recommandation atelier : Estimated repair: 60€ - 350€ (0.5h - 2h labor). DIY feasible with standard tools.

title: P00C6: P00C6 - Fuel Rail Pressure Too Low - Engine Cranking
content: CODE DÉFAUT OBD-II [P00C6] : P00C6 - Fuel Rail Pressure Too Low - Engine Cranking. Système : Powertrain (Engine & Transmission). Description technique : Direct-injection engines release injection only once the rail has reached a minimum pressure. P00C6 is set when this pressure is not reached quickly enough while cranking, or, in another documented variant, when it drops below the minimum again right after the high-pressure start. Cranking then takes longer or the engine does not start. The check runs once per start; some manufacturers only enable it above a minimum tank level. Causes fréquentes : High-pressure pump weak, or its drive cam or follower worn [HIGH], Lift pump or low-pressure supply too weak [MEDIUM], Control valve on the pump faulty [MEDIUM], Leak or check valve fault letting pressure bleed off after shutdown [MEDIUM]. title: P00C7: P00C7 - Intake Air Pressure Measurement System - Multiple Sensor Correlation Bank 1
content: CODE DÉFAUT OBD-II [P00C7] : P00C7 - Intake Air Pressure Measurement System - Multiple Sensor Correlation Bank 1. Système : Powertrain (Engine & Transmission). Description technique : With the engine stopped, all pressure sensors in the intake system (manifold pressure, boost pressure, barometric pressure) should read ambient pressure; some diesels also compare them at idle. The control module compares them: if one sensor stands out, it sets that sensor's own code. P00C7 is set when the readings disagree but no single sensor can be identified as faulty, which points to a fault affecting several sensors, such as a shared reference voltage or ground. Causes fréquentes : Shared 5 V reference or ground of the pressure sensors disturbed [HIGH], Two sensors drifting at the same time (contamination, oil mist, ageing) [MEDIUM], Pressure hose to a sensor leaking or blocked [MEDIUM], Engine control module or software [LOW]. Urgence : Urgent / Danger. Recommandation atelier : Estimated repair: 50€ - 300€ (0.5h - 2h labor). DIY feasible with standard tools.

title: P00C8: P00C8 - Fuel Pressure Regulator A Solenoid Supply Voltage Control Circuit/Open
content: CODE DÉFAUT OBD-II [P00C8] : P00C8 - Fuel Pressure Regulator A Solenoid Supply Voltage Control Circuit/Open. Système : Powertrain (Engine & Transmission). Description technique : Some engine control modules switch the solenoid of fuel pressure regulator A on both sides: the ground side is monitored by P0090 to P0092, the supply side (high-side driver) by P00C8 to P00CA. On gasoline direct injection the regulator is typically the control valve on the high-pressure pump. P00C8 reports an open circuit on the supply side. Rail pressure can then not be controlled, causing starting problems, stalling or reduced power. Causes fréquentes : Supply wire or connector to the pump solenoid damaged by heat or chafing [HIGH], Solenoid coil open [MEDIUM], High-side driver in the engine control module faulty [LOW]. Urgence : Urgent / Danger. Recommandation atelier : Estimated repair: 50€ - 2000€ (0.5h - 3h labor). DIY feasible with standard tools.

title: P00CB: P00CB - Fuel Volume Regulator Solenoid Supply Voltage Control Circuit/Open
content: CODE DÉFAUT OBD-II [P00CB] : P00CB - Fuel Volume Regulator Solenoid Supply Voltage Control Circuit/Open. Système : Powertrain (Engine & Transmission). Description technique : The fuel volume regulator is the solenoid valve that meters how much fuel the high-pressure pump delivers (metering unit on diesels, pump control valve on some gasoline direct-injection engines). Many control modules switch such solenoids on both sides; P0001 to P0004 cover the control side, while these codes cover the supply side (high-side driver). P00CB reports an open circuit on the supply side. Rail pressure may then deviate, with reduced power or hard starting. None of the published manufacturer documents searched uses this code; the explanation follows regulations and comparable manufacturer monitors. title: P00CE: P00CE - Intake Air Temperature Measurement System - Multiple Sensor Correlation Bank 1
content: CODE DÉFAUT OBD-II [P00CE] : P00CE - Intake Air Temperature Measurement System - Multiple Sensor Correlation Bank 1. Système : Powertrain (Engine & Transmission). Description technique : After a long standstill (six hours in a documented case) all intake air temperature sensors, for example intake air, charge air cooler and manifold temperature, should read about the same. The control module compares them in pairs: if one sensor stands out, it sets that sensor's own plausibility code. This code is set when no pair agrees, so no single sensor can be identified as faulty. A detected engine preheater suspends the test. Since it runs only after a long standstill, the code may take a night to return after being cleared. Some vehicles also disable start-stop while this code is stored. title: P00D1: P00D1 - HO2S Heater Control Circuit Range/Performance Bank 1 Sensor 1
content: CODE DÉFAUT OBD-II [P00D1] : P00D1 - HO2S Heater Control Circuit Range/Performance Bank 1 Sensor 1. Système : Powertrain (Engine & Transmission). Description technique : This code concerns the heated oxygen sensor upstream of the catalytic converter (sensor 1) on bank 1. Unlike the heater circuit codes, which report an open or short circuit, this code means the heater is driven but does not bring the oxygen sensor to the expected temperature. One documented method, used where no current-measuring shunt is fitted, measures the internal impedance of the sensor element: a hot element has a low impedance. If the impedance stays above a limit that depends on the calculated element temperature and the voltage at the sensor connector, the heating is judged insufficient. The test runs once per trip. Typical causes are an aged heating element or added resistance from corrosion in the heater circuit. For this sensor position no manufacturer description of the test was found; the code appears in a manufacturer's code list, and the explanation follows the documented counterpart for sensor 2. Causes fréquentes : Heating element aged, resistance increased [HIGH], Corrosion or contact resistance at connector or harness of the heater circuit [HIGH], Too low supply voltage at the sensor connector, e.g. poor ground [MEDIUM], Diagnostic software (manufacturer updates exist for some vehicles) [MEDIUM]. Urgence : High. Recommandation atelier : Estimated repair: 50€ - 300€ (0.5h - 1.5h labor). DIY feasible with standard tools.

title: P00D5: P00D5 - HO2S Sensor Correlation Bank 1 Sensor 1/Bank 1 Sensor 2
content: CODE DÉFAUT OBD-II [P00D5] : P00D5 - HO2S Sensor Correlation Bank 1 Sensor 1/Bank 1 Sensor 2. Système : Powertrain (Engine & Transmission). Description technique : During fuel cut-off on overrun the exhaust gas is pure air, so the oxygen sensors before and behind the catalytic converter must both report the same lean value. A documented method averages and normalises the signals of both sensors during fuel cut-off and sets the code when they differ by more than a limit; it runs once per drive cycle and needs several overrun phases. The code points to one of the sensors having drifted, not to the catalytic converter. The manufacturer documenting it uses wide-band sensors in both positions. Causes fréquentes : Upstream sensor aged or shifted [HIGH], Downstream sensor aged or shifted [HIGH], Air or exhaust leak between the sensors falsifying the lean signal [MEDIUM], Retrofitted sensor with wrong characteristic, or software [LOW]. Urgence : High. Recommandation atelier : Estimated repair: 200€ - 700€ (1h - 2h labor). DIY feasible with standard tools.

title: P00D7: P00D7 - Turbocharger/Supercharger Bypass Valve A Temperature Too High
content: CODE DÉFAUT OBD-II [P00D7] : P00D7 - Turbocharger/Supercharger Bypass Valve A Temperature Too High. Système : Powertrain (Engine & Transmission). Description technique : Bypass valve A is the electric compressor recirculation valve, mounted close to the hot compressor and turbine housing. This code reports that its temperature is too high. How the temperature is detected is not described in published manufacturer documents; a documented principle for comparable turbocharger solenoids estimates the coil temperature from current, supply voltage and duty cycle and protects the coil by limiting or switching it off. With the valve switched off, the compressor may surge when lifting off the throttle. None of the published manufacturer documents searched uses this code; the explanation follows regulations and comparable manufacturer monitors. Causes fréquentes : Valve energised for unusually long periods, e.g. due to boost control problems [MEDIUM], Coil with shorted turns or aged [MEDIUM], Heat shield missing or exhaust leak near the turbocharger [MEDIUM], Contact resistance or supply fault distorting the estimate [LOW]. Urgence : Urgent / Danger. Recommandation atelier : Estimated repair: 40€ - 250€ (0.5h - 1.5h labor). DIY feasible with standard tools.

title: P00DE: P00DE - Charge Air Cooler Coolant Temperature Sensor A Circuit
content: CODE DÉFAUT OBD-II [P00DE] : P00DE - Charge Air Cooler Coolant Temperature Sensor A Circuit. Système : Powertrain (Engine & Transmission). Description technique : With indirect charge air cooling, a water-to-air charge air cooler cools the charge air; it sits in a separate low-temperature coolant circuit with an electric pump and its own radiator. The charge air cooler coolant temperature sensor A measures the coolant temperature of this circuit. The control module uses it to control the pump and to monitor cooling performance. Documented users are diesel engines from Ford and GM. P00DE: This is the general circuit fault; low and high signals have their own codes. No manufacturer description naming this exact code was found. Description technique : With indirect charge air cooling, a water-to-air charge air cooler cools the charge air; it sits in a separate low-temperature coolant circuit with an electric pump and its own radiator. The charge air cooler coolant temperature sensor A measures the coolant temperature of this circuit. The control module uses it to control the pump and to monitor cooling performance. Documented users are diesel engines from Ford and GM. P00E2: The signal jumps or drops out briefly, which typically points to a loose contact or a chafed harness. Causes fréquentes : Wiring harness chafed or fuse blown (documented by manufacturer bulletins) [HIGH], Sensor faulty [HIGH], Connector corroded or water ingress [MEDIUM], Engine control module faulty [LOW]. Urgence : Urgent / Danger. Recommandation atelier : Estimated repair: 100€ - 300€ (0.5h - 1.5h labor). DIY feasible with standard tools.

title: P00E3: P00E3 - Exhaust Heat Exchanger Exhaust Bypass Valve A Stuck Open
content: CODE DÉFAUT OBD-II [P00E3] : P00E3 - Exhaust Heat Exchanger Exhaust Bypass Valve A Stuck Open. Système : Powertrain (Engine & Transmission). Description technique : Some engines, mainly hybrids and fuel-saving designs, have an exhaust heat exchanger behind the catalytic converter that transfers exhaust heat into the coolant for faster warm-up of engine and cabin. A bypass valve sends the exhaust either through the heat exchanger or around it. Documented diagnostics compare the coolant temperature rise at the heat exchanger with the commanded mode: if it behaves like bypass while recovery is commanded, or the other way round, the valve is considered stuck. P00E3 reports the valve stuck open. How "open" and "closed" map to bypass and recovery is not publicly documented, so both possible effects should be considered: slow warm-up and weak heating, or excessive coolant heat. None of the published manufacturer documents searched uses this code; the explanation follows regulations and comparable manufacturer monitors. Causes fréquentes : Valve flap coked or corroded and sticking [HIGH], Actuator faulty (electric or vacuum) [MEDIUM], Linkage or return spring broken [MEDIUM], Heat exchanger temperature sensor faulty, simulating a stuck valve [LOW]. Urgence : High. Recommandation atelier : Estimated repair: 150€ - 1500€ (1h - 4h labor). Professional workshop recommended.
source_name: SAE J2012 / ISO 15031-6 Standard OBD-II Database

title: P00E5: P00E5 - Intake Air Temperature/Fuel Temperature Correlation
content: CODE DÉFAUT OBD-II [P00E5] : P00E5 - Intake Air Temperature/Fuel Temperature Correlation. Système : Powertrain (Engine & Transmission). Description technique : After a long standstill, intake air and fuel should be at about ambient temperature. This code is set when the intake air and fuel temperature sensors differ too much at the next start; it does not say which sensor is wrong. A detected engine block heater usually suspends the test. One manufacturer performs the same comparison under another code; who uses this exact code could not be documented. Causes fréquentes : Fuel or intake air temperature sensor drifting [HIGH], Block heater, sunshine, very warm or cold fuel from refuelling, or a short standstill [MEDIUM], Contact resistance at a connector [MEDIUM], Engine control module or software [LOW]. Urgence : High. Recommandation atelier : Estimated repair: 60€ - 250€ (0.5h - 1.5h labor). DIY feasible with standard tools.

title: P00E6: P00E6 - Intake Air Pressure Measurement System - Multiple Sensor Correlation Bank 2
content: CODE DÉFAUT OBD-II [P00E6] : P00E6 - Intake Air Pressure Measurement System - Multiple Sensor Correlation Bank 2. Système : Powertrain (Engine & Transmission). Description technique : This is the bank 2 counterpart of the multiple pressure sensor check for engines with separate pressure measurement per bank, such as twin-turbo V engines. With the engine stopped, all intake pressure sensors should read ambient pressure. If one stands out, it gets its own code; this code is set when the readings disagree but no single sensor can be identified, which points to a fault affecting several sensors such as a shared reference voltage or ground. None of the published manufacturer documents searched uses this code; the explanation follows regulations and comparable manufacturer monitors. Causes fréquentes : A pressure sensor on bank 2 drifting [HIGH], Shared 5 V reference or ground faulty [MEDIUM], Sensor port blocked or hose leaking [MEDIUM], Barometric sensor drifting [LOW]. Urgence : Urgent / Danger. Recommandation atelier : Estimated repair: 40€ - 300€ (0.5h - 1.5h labor). DIY feasible with standard tools.

title: P00E7: P00E7 - Intake Air Temperature Measurement System - Multiple Sensor Correlation Bank 2
content: CODE DÉFAUT OBD-II [P00E7] : P00E7 - Intake Air Temperature Measurement System - Multiple Sensor Correlation Bank 2. Système : Powertrain (Engine & Transmission). Description technique : After a long standstill (six hours in a documented case) all intake air temperature sensors, for example intake air, charge air cooler and manifold temperature, should read about the same. The control module compares them in pairs: if one sensor stands out, it sets that sensor's own plausibility code. This code is set when no pair agrees, so no single sensor can be identified as faulty. A detected engine preheater suspends the test. Since it runs only after a long standstill, the code may take a night to return after being cleared. No manufacturer description naming this exact code was found; bank 2 codes are intended for engines with two separate intake paths. Causes fréquentes : One temperature sensor drifting without setting its own code [MEDIUM], Uneven cooling, undetected preheater or strong sunshine [MEDIUM], Shared ground or reference line disturbed, falsifying several sensors [MEDIUM], Engine control module or software [LOW]. Urgence : High. Recommandation atelier : Estimated repair: 50€ - 300€ (0.5h - 1.5h labor). DIY feasible with standard tools.

title: P00E8: P00E8 - Intake Air Temperature Sensor 3 Circuit Bank 1
content: CODE DÉFAUT OBD-II [P00E8] : P00E8 - Intake Air Temperature Sensor 3 Circuit Bank 1. Système : Powertrain (Engine & Transmission). Description technique : Intake air temperature sensor 3 is a third air temperature sensor in the intake path. On documented turbocharged engines with a humidity sensor it is the manifold temperature sensor behind the charge air cooler, an NTC thermistor read directly by the engine control module and used for cylinder filling and ignition timing. The numbering of intake air temperature sensors differs between manufacturers. P00E8: This is the general circuit fault; low and high signals have their own codes. title: P00F2: P00F2 - Humidity Sensor Circuit/Open
content: CODE DÉFAUT OBD-II [P00F2] : P00F2 - Humidity Sensor Circuit/Open. Système : Powertrain (Engine & Transmission). Description technique : The humidity sensor measures the relative humidity of the intake air; on documented vehicles it is built into the mass air flow sensor or a combined sensor. The engine control module uses the value, for example, to correct torque and in emission models. One documented design is capacitive and reports humidity as a pulsed signal with a duty cycle that the control module converts back. P00F2 reports an open or general circuit fault of the humidity sensor. No manufacturer description naming this exact code was found. Causes fréquentes : Connector or wire interrupted [HIGH], Sensor or combined air flow sensor faulty [MEDIUM]. Urgence : High. Recommandation atelier : Estimated repair: 80€ - 450€ (0.3h - 1h labor). title: P00F7: P00F7 - Barometric Pressure - Turbocharger/Supercharger Inlet Pressure Correlation Bank 2
content: CODE DÉFAUT OBD-II [P00F7] : P00F7 - Barometric Pressure - Turbocharger/Supercharger Inlet Pressure Correlation Bank 2. Système : Powertrain (Engine & Transmission). Description technique : This is the bank 2 counterpart of the comparison between barometric pressure and the pressure ahead of the turbocharger or supercharger. At low air flow the inlet pressure sensor reads close to ambient pressure, minus the small loss across the air filter, so it must match the barometric reading. The code is set when the difference is too large; a clogged air filter or a leaking intake hose on bank 2 can cause it as well as a drifting sensor. None of the published manufacturer documents searched uses this code; the explanation follows regulations and comparable manufacturer monitors. Causes fréquentes : Inlet pressure sensor of bank 2 drifting or dirty [HIGH], Air filter or intake of bank 2 clogged [MEDIUM], Intake hose between air flow meter and turbocharger leaking or slipped off [MEDIUM], Barometric sensor faulty [LOW]. Urgence : Urgent / Danger. Recommandation atelier : Estimated repair: 20€ - 200€ (0.3h - 1h labor). DIY feasible with standard tools.

title: P00F8: P00F8 - Turbocharger Outlet Pressure Sensor A Circuit
content: CODE DÉFAUT OBD-II [P00F8] : P00F8 - Turbocharger Outlet Pressure Sensor A Circuit. Système : Powertrain (Engine & Transmission). Description technique : The turbocharger outlet pressure sensor A measures the pressure directly at the compressor outlet. It is a separate code family from the boost pressure sensor, which usually measures the pressure just ahead of the throttle; engines use it where the pressure behind the compressor is needed in addition, for example to judge the pressure loss across the charge air cooler or to protect against compressor surge. One manufacturer documents it as a combined temperature and pressure sensor. P00F8 is the general circuit fault of this sensor. None of the published manufacturer documents searched uses this code; the explanation follows regulations and comparable manufacturer monitors. Causes fréquentes : Connector loose or not fully engaged, or sensor not seated properly [HIGH], Wire interrupted, short to ground or 5 V reference missing [HIGH], Leak at the sensor flange or seal [MEDIUM], Engine control module faulty [LOW]. title: P00F9: P00F9 - Turbocharger Outlet Pressure Sensor A Range/Performance

title: P00FB: P00FB - Turbocharger Outlet Pressure Sensor A Circuit High
content: CODE DÉFAUT OBD-II [P00FB] : P00FB - Turbocharger Outlet Pressure Sensor A Circuit High. Système : Powertrain (Engine & Transmission). Description technique : The turbocharger outlet pressure sensor A measures the pressure directly after the compressor, usually ahead of the charge air cooler; FCA fits it as a combined temperature and pressure sensor. Boost control and compressor protection use the value. P00FB means the signal voltage is above its valid range: typically a signal wire shorted to the 5 V reference or battery voltage, an open ground, or a failed sensor. It does not mean the boost really is too high – that would be P0234. The circuit is monitored continuously from key-on; comparable GM pressure sensors fail above 86–97 % of the reference for about 4 s. The engine then works with a substitute value and may limit boost. GM and Ford do not use this code family in their published summaries – they rely on the boost sensor ahead of the throttle (P0235–P0238) – so no manufacturer document naming exactly this code was found. Causes fréquentes : Signal wire shorted to 5 V reference or battery voltage [HIGH], Ground (low reference) wire open or connector corroded [MEDIUM], Sensor faulty internally (oil mist, heat at compressor outlet) [MEDIUM], Engine control module faulty [LOW]. title: P00FC: P00FC - Turbocharger Outlet Pressure Sensor A Intermittent/Erratic

title: P00FD: P00FD - Battery B State of Charge Performance
content: CODE DÉFAUT OBD-II [P00FD] : P00FD - Battery B State of Charge Performance. Système : Powertrain (Engine & Transmission). Description technique : 'Battery B' here is not a hybrid high-voltage battery (those have codes from P0B27) but, in the only documented use by FCA/Stellantis, the 12 V auxiliary battery of the start-stop system. When the engine restarts automatically, a relay separates main and auxiliary battery so that the auxiliary one keeps the control units stable while the main battery cranks. The engine module sets P00FD if the auxiliary battery is disconnected on the first start, drops below about 8 V during an auto-start, or repeatedly falls below 10.3 V (counter reaches ten). Start-stop is then disabled; often it follows a jump start or many short trips. Whether the MIL comes on is not stated in the sources. Causes fréquentes : Auxiliary battery discharged or aged [HIGH], Loose or corroded positive or ground connections at either battery [HIGH], 150 A fuse or fuse array in the power distribution centre open or poorly contacting [MEDIUM], Battery separation relay stuck [LOW]. Urgence : Moderate. Recommandation atelier : Estimated repair: 0€ - 250€ (0.3h - 1.5h labor). DIY feasible with standard tools.

title: P00FE: P00FE - EVAP System Tank Vapor Line Restricted/Blocked
content: CODE DÉFAUT OBD-II [P00FE] : P00FE - EVAP System Tank Vapor Line Restricted/Blocked. Système : Powertrain (Engine & Transmission). Description technique : The evaporative emission system stores fuel vapour from the tank in a charcoal canister and later purges it into the engine. P00FE means the vapour path between tank and canister is restricted or blocked. That matters because a blocked line can hide the tank side from the leak test and disturb tank venting and refuelling. Ford, where P00FE replaces its own code P144A, checks this once per drive cycle during the cruise leak test, while purging with the vent valve closed, and confirms suspicious pressure responses with an intrusive test. VW used the same code on the 2013–2019 Golf, where the diagnosis covers the purge valve and the leak detection module. Typical causes are kinked or pinched lines and charcoal grains from a broken canister. Causes fréquentes : Kinked, pinched or misrouted vapour line between tank and canister [HIGH], Charcoal canister broken down, grains blocking lines or valves [MEDIUM], Rollover or fill-limit valve at the tank stuck closed (e.g. after overfilling) [MEDIUM], Purge valve or leak detection module faulty [LOW]. Urgence : High. Recommandation atelier : Estimated repair: 80€ - 600€ (0.5h - 3h labor). Professional workshop recommended.

title: P00FF: P00FF - Body Control Module Requested MIL Illumination
content: CODE DÉFAUT OBD-II [P00FF] : P00FF - Body Control Module Requested MIL Illumination. Système : Powertrain (Engine & Transmission). Description technique : P00FF is an information code in the engine control module: the body control module has detected an emissions-relevant fault of its own and asks over the data bus for the check engine light. The engine module stores P00FF so that a generic OBD scanner can see why the MIL is on; the actual fault is stored in the body control module as B or U codes and must be read there. GM documents two cases – a 2020 Cadillac CT5 with climate flap actuator codes and 2025 full-size SUVs with U1962 – both cured by reprogramming the body control module, not by replacing parts. The mechanism matches other 'module requested MIL' codes such as P069E. P00FF itself causes no limp mode. Causes fréquentes : Emissions-relevant fault in the body control module or its sensors/actuators (own B/U codes) [HIGH], Software or calibration fault in the body control module [MEDIUM], Communication fault on the data bus [LOW], Engine control module faulty [LOW]. Urgence : High. Recommandation atelier : Estimated repair: 0€ - 300€ (0.3h - 1.5h labor). Professional workshop recommended.

title: P0100: P0100 - Mass or Volume Air Flow Sensor A Circuit
content: CODE DÉFAUT OBD-II [P0100] : P0100 - Mass or Volume Air Flow Sensor A Circuit. Système : Powertrain (Engine & Transmission). Description technique : The mass air flow sensor (MAF) sits between the air filter and the throttle or compressor and measures how much air the engine draws in; fuel quantity, load and ignition are calculated from it. Most are hot-film or hot-wire sensors that output either a voltage or, on GM, Saab and newer Ford systems, a frequency. P0100 means the control module gets no usable signal at all. Ford uses it for a broken sensing element on digital sensors (period longer than 1.3 ms, i.e. below about 0.78 kHz, for half a second); on GM's 3.0 V6 in the Saab 9-4X it is set at 0 Hz. Many systems with voltage sensors skip P0100 and report low or high directly. The engine then runs on air mass calculated from manifold pressure, throttle angle and speed; Ford also disables start-stop. Causes fréquentes : Connector unplugged or corroded, signal or supply wire open [HIGH], Sensor faulty internally (broken element, failed electronics) [HIGH], Supply fuse or relay failed [MEDIUM], Control module input faulty [LOW]. Urgence : Urgent / Danger. Recommandation atelier : Estimated repair: 20€ - 300€ (0.3h - 1.5h labor). DIY feasible with standard tools.

title: P0105: P0105 - Manifold Absolute Pressure/Barometric Pressure Sensor Circuit
content: CODE DÉFAUT OBD-II [P0105] : P0105 - Manifold Absolute Pressure/Barometric Pressure Sensor Circuit. Système : Powertrain (Engine & Transmission). Description technique : The manifold absolute pressure (MAP) sensor measures the pressure behind the throttle; on vehicles without a separate barometric sensor it also supplies the ambient pressure, read at key-on or wide-open throttle – hence 'MAP/BARO'. It is a three-wire sensor with 5 V reference, ground and signal. P0105 is the general circuit fault and is rarely used today: most petrol engines report low, high and intermittent separately (P0107–P0109). It appears mainly where the fault cannot be broken down further – Ford's 2023 diesels set it when the digital SENT sensor reports a bad status or an out-of-limit value for 5 s (lost communication is a separate U code), and Bosch EDC16 diesels use it with a fault type byte, for example signal below 0.2 V. Saab then substitutes 101.3 kPa, limits torque and switches off EGR and boost control. Causes fréquentes : Connector or wiring to the sensor open, shorted or loose [HIGH], MAP sensor faulty (oiled, failed internally, SENT status fault) [MEDIUM], Sensor hose disconnected, vacuum or boost leak [MEDIUM], 5 V reference pulled down by another sensor on the same circuit [LOW]. Urgence : Urgent / Danger. Recommandation atelier : Estimated repair: 20€ - 200€ (0.3h - 1h labor). DIY feasible with standard tools.

title: P0106: P0106 - Manifold Absolute Pressure/Barometric Pressure Sensor Circuit Range/Performance
content: CODE DÉFAUT OBD-II [P0106] : P0106 - Manifold Absolute Pressure/Barometric Pressure Sensor Circuit Range/Performance. Système : Powertrain (Engine & Transmission). Description technique : The manifold absolute pressure (MAP) sensor measures the pressure behind the throttle; on vehicles without a separate barometric sensor it also supplies the ambient pressure, read at key-on or wide-open throttle – hence 'MAP/BARO'. It is a three-wire sensor with 5 V reference, ground and signal. P0106 is a plausibility fault: the signal is electrically valid but implausible – stuck, offset or drifting. Two tests are common. With the engine stopped, all pressures equalise, so MAP must match ambient (and boost) pressure; Ford allows 1.5–3 inHg. While running, MAP is compared with a value modelled from air mass, throttle and speed – GM blames the MAP sensor above about 23–30 kPa error, with two trips on petrol and one on diesel. Turbo engines with three sensors find the odd one out by majority. Besides the sensor, intake or boost leaks often cause it. Causes fréquentes : Vacuum leak at the intake manifold or boost leak (hose, clamp, charge air cooler) [HIGH], Sensor oiled or sooted, port blocked (EGR soot), characteristic drifted [HIGH], High resistance in signal, reference or ground wire [MEDIUM], Comparison sensor wrong, or mechanical cause (dirty throttle, EGR stuck open) [MEDIUM]. title: P010A: P010A - Mass or Volume Air Flow Sensor B Circuit
content: CODE DÉFAUT OBD-II [P010A] : P010A - Mass or Volume Air Flow Sensor B Circuit. Système : Powertrain (Engine & Transmission). title: P010B: P010B - Mass or Volume Air Flow Sensor B Circuit Range/Performance
content: CODE DÉFAUT OBD-II [P010B] : P010B - Mass or Volume Air Flow Sensor B Circuit Range/Performance. Système : Powertrain (Engine & Transmission). Description technique : Sensor B is a second mass air flow sensor in a second intake path, found on engines with two air filter boxes – for example the Nissan VR30DDTT twin-turbo V6 (where sensor B belongs to bank 2) or GM's 3.0 litre twin-turbo V6. P010B is the plausibility fault of sensor B: the signal is electrically valid but does not fit. GM checks it like sensor A against a model built from the other sensors (manifold pressure, boost, throttle, sensor A) and fails it above 20 g/s deviation, with two trips. For the VR30DDTT Nissan names a loose or leaking left-hand intake pipe as the main cause and warns against touching or dismantling the sensor. Other causes match P0101: a soiled element, a clogged filter on that side or a boost leak. title: P010F: P010F - Mass or Volume Air Flow Sensor A/B Correlation
content: CODE DÉFAUT OBD-II [P010F] : P010F - Mass or Volume Air Flow Sensor A/B Correlation. Système : Powertrain (Engine & Transmission). Description technique : Engines with two intake paths have two mass air flow sensors, A and B. On a symmetrical V engine both sides should draw about the same amount of air, so the readings can be compared with each other. P010F is set when both signals are electrically valid but differ by more than allowed; the code does not say which side is wrong. No manufacturer document using exactly this code or its threshold was found: GM's twin-turbo V6 and Nissan's VR30DDTT assess each sensor separately against a model (P0101/P010B). The description therefore rests on the CARB requirement for plausibility checks and on component sources for engines with two sensors. Typical causes are a leaking intake pipe or a soiled sensor on one side. title: P0110: P0110 - Intake Air Temperature Sensor 1 Circuit Bank 1
content: CODE DÉFAUT OBD-II [P0110] : P0110 - Intake Air Temperature Sensor 1 Circuit Bank 1. Système : Powertrain (Engine & Transmission). Description technique : Intake air temperature sensor 1 is the first air temperature sensor in the intake path; depending on the vehicle it is built into the mass air flow sensor, mounted near the air filter or, on some naturally aspirated GM engines, fitted in the intake manifold. Most versions are NTC thermistors in a 5 V divider: the hotter the air, the lower the signal voltage. P0110 is the general circuit fault. With a conventional analogue sensor most manufacturers report low and high signals separately (P0112/P0113), so P0110 mainly appears in two cases: with digital (SENT) sensors that combine air mass and temperature, where it stands for lost communication or an implausible status (Ford diesel 2023, after about 5 s), and in some Bosch systems as a collective code whose fault type byte tells open circuit from short to ground. The control module then uses a substitute temperature; some systems also limit torque. Causes fréquentes : Connector or wiring to the sensor open or corroded [HIGH], Sensor or mass air flow sensor with built-in temperature sensor faulty [HIGH], Sensor supply or ground disturbed [MEDIUM], Engine control module faulty [LOW]. Urgence : Urgent / Danger. Recommandation atelier : Estimated repair: 40€ - 300€ (0.3h - 1.5h labor). DIY feasible with standard tools.

title: P0111: P0111 - Intake Air Temperature Sensor 1 Circuit Range/Performance Bank 1
content: CODE DÉFAUT OBD-II [P0111] : P0111 - Intake Air Temperature Sensor 1 Circuit Range/Performance Bank 1. Système : Powertrain (Engine & Transmission). Description technique : Intake air temperature sensor 1 is the first air temperature sensor in the intake path; depending on the vehicle it is built into the mass air flow sensor, mounted near the air filter or, on some naturally aspirated GM engines, fitted in the intake manifold. Most versions are NTC thermistors in a 5 V divider: the hotter the air, the lower the signal voltage. P0111 is a plausibility fault: the signal is electrically valid but does not fit. The usual test runs at key-on after a long soak (Ford 6 h, GM 8 h): the intake air sensor is compared with other temperature sensors such as coolant, cylinder head, charge air cooler or IAT2, which should all read about the same. GM flags it above about 25 °C deviation, Ford above about 17 °C; Ford first confirms with a drive above 40 mph because sunshine can warm a sensor, and also sets P0111 if the air reads over 66 °C while driving. A detected block heater suspends the test. Two consecutive trips are needed. title: P0113: P0113 - Intake Air Temperature Sensor 1 Circuit High Bank 1
content: CODE DÉFAUT OBD-II [P0113] : P0113 - Intake Air Temperature Sensor 1 Circuit High Bank 1. Système : Powertrain (Engine & Transmission). Description technique : Intake air temperature sensor 1 is the first air temperature sensor in the intake path; depending on the vehicle it is built into the mass air flow sensor, mounted near the air filter or, on some naturally aspirated GM engines, fitted in the intake manifold. title: P0114: P0114 - Intake Air Temperature Sensor 1 Circuit Intermittent/Erratic Bank 1
content: CODE DÉFAUT OBD-II [P0114] : P0114 - Intake Air Temperature Sensor 1 Circuit Intermittent/Erratic Bank 1. Système : Powertrain (Engine & Transmission). Description technique : Intake air temperature sensor 1 is the first air temperature sensor in the intake path; depending on the vehicle it is built into the mass air flow sensor, mounted near the air filter or, on some naturally aspirated GM engines, fitted in the intake manifold. Most versions are NTC thermistors in a 5 V divider: the hotter the air, the lower the signal voltage. P0114 covers an unsteady signal. Air temperature changes slowly, so rapid jumps point to the wiring rather than the air. Ford counts short excursions out of range that are each too brief for P0112/P0113 and sets the code after ten of them in one drive cycle. GM evaluates noise within the valid range: if the readings taken every 100 ms add up to more than 80 °C of movement within one second, in four of five seconds, the sample counts as failed. GM needs two trips. Typical culprit is a loose contact that opens with engine movement. title: P0115: P0115 - Engine Coolant Temperature Sensor 1 Circuit
content: CODE DÉFAUT OBD-II [P0115] : P0115 - Engine Coolant Temperature Sensor 1 Circuit. Système : Powertrain (Engine & Transmission). Description technique : The engine coolant temperature sensor 1 is an NTC thermistor: the control module feeds 5 V through a resistor, and as the coolant warms the resistance and signal voltage fall. Its value drives cold-start enrichment, idle speed, ignition timing, the radiator fan and the release of closed-loop mixture control. Some Ford engines measure cylinder head temperature instead and calculate a coolant value from it. P0115 is the general circuit fault without telling low from high. Today it has largely been replaced by P0117, P0118 and P0119; GM and Ford do not set it in the tables checked. Older or individual systems still use it as a collective code, for example Saab Trionic T5 (1998). The circuit is monitored continuously; when it fails, the module uses a substitute value and many systems run the radiator fan permanently. Causes fréquentes : Connector corroded or loose, terminal spread [HIGH], Broken or chafed signal or ground wire [MEDIUM], Sensor faulty internally (short, open, coolant inside) [MEDIUM], Control module input or 5 V supply faulty [LOW]. Urgence : Urgent / Danger. Recommandation atelier : Estimated repair: 20€ - 150€ (0.3h - 1.5h labor). DIY feasible with standard tools.

title: P0116: P0116 - Engine Coolant Temperature Sensor 1 Circuit Range/Performance
content: CODE DÉFAUT OBD-II [P0116] : P0116 - Engine Coolant Temperature Sensor 1 Circuit Range/Performance. Système : Powertrain (Engine & Transmission). Description technique : The engine coolant temperature sensor 1 is an NTC thermistor: the control module feeds 5 V through a resistor, and as the coolant warms the resistance and signal voltage fall. Its value drives cold-start enrichment, idle speed, ignition timing, the radiator fan and the release of closed-loop mixture control. Some Ford engines measure cylinder head temperature instead and calculate a coolant value from it. P0116 is a plausibility fault: the signal is electrically valid but not believable. Most often it checks for a sensor stuck too warm. After a long soak (GM 8 h, Ford 6 h) coolant must be close to intake air temperature; GM fails it above about 19 °C difference without a detected block heater, Ford if it reads over 110 °C or sits at 79–110 °C. Ford diesels instead check whether coolant warms fast enough in frost. A sensor stuck warm suppresses cold-start enrichment and can defeat the thermostat monitor, which is why CARB requires this test. GM uses one or two trips depending on the engine. Causes fréquentes : Sensor drifting and reading too warm (ageing, coolant ingress) [HIGH], Corrosion or contact resistance in connector or wiring [MEDIUM], Block heater or preheater not detected [MEDIUM], Comparison sensor (intake air, ambient) wrong [LOW]. title: P0117: P0117 - Engine Coolant Temperature Sensor 1 Circuit Low
content: CODE DÉFAUT OBD-II [P0117] : P0117 - Engine Coolant Temperature Sensor 1 Circuit Low. Système : Powertrain (Engine & Transmission). Description technique : The engine coolant temperature sensor 1 is an NTC thermistor: the control module feeds 5 V through a resistor, and as the coolant warms the resistance and signal voltage fall. Its value drives cold-start enrichment, idle speed, ignition timing, the radiator fan and the release of closed-loop mixture control. Some Ford engines measure cylinder head temperature instead and calculate a coolant value from it. P0117 means the signal voltage is too low, so the sensor would report an implausibly hot engine (around 140–160 °C). content: CODE DÉFAUT OBD-II [P0118] : P0118 - Engine Coolant Temperature Sensor 1 Circuit High. Système : Powertrain (Engine & Transmission). Description technique : The engine coolant temperature sensor 1 is an NTC thermistor: the control module feeds 5 V through a resistor, and as the coolant warms the resistance and signal voltage fall. title: P0119: P0119 - Engine Coolant Temperature Sensor 1 Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
content: CODE DÉFAUT OBD-II [P0119] : P0119 - Engine Coolant Temperature Sensor 1 Circuit Intermittent/Erratic. Système : Powertrain (Engine & Transmission). Description technique : The engine coolant temperature sensor 1 is an NTC thermistor: the control module feeds 5 V through a resistor, and as the coolant warms the resistance and signal voltage fall. Its value drives cold-start enrichment, idle speed, ignition timing, the radiator fan and the release of closed-loop mixture control. Some Ford engines measure cylinder head temperature instead and calculate a coolant value from it. Coolant temperature can only change slowly because of the thermal mass involved. P0119 is set when the reading jumps faster than physically possible. GM calculates, every second, a window for the next valid value from the previous reading and a sensor time constant of 13 s; readings outside it in three of four samples count as a fault, monitored continuously over two trips. GM/Saab set it after more than 4 s of abrupt changes and then run the radiator fan. Typical causes are loose contacts or a harness chafing as the engine moves. title: P011A: P011A - Engine Coolant Temperature Sensor 1/2 Correlation
content: CODE DÉFAUT OBD-II [P011A] : P011A - Engine Coolant Temperature Sensor 1/2 Correlation. Système : Powertrain (Engine & Transmission). Description technique : Some engines have two coolant temperature sensors that check each other. P011A is set when both are electrically fine but their readings differ more than a calibrated amount under conditions where they should agree. Mazda documents the code for the 2013–2016 CX-5 and 2014–2016 Mazda6: sensor 2 sits in the heater hose, and a clogged heater core keeps it noticeably colder, so P011A often comes with weak cabin heat although both sensors are good. Mazda's check is to compare both sensors with ambient temperature after an overnight soak and then the temperature difference across the heater hoses. A block heater used below 0 °C can also trigger it. Causes fréquentes : Clogged heater core or restricted coolant flow at sensor 2 [HIGH], One of the two sensors drifting [MEDIUM], Air in the cooling system or low coolant level [MEDIUM], Block heater use in frost [LOW]. title: P011B: P011B - Engine Coolant Temperature/Intake Air Temperature Correlation
content: CODE DÉFAUT OBD-II [P011B] : P011B - Engine Coolant Temperature/Intake Air Temperature Correlation. Système : Powertrain (Engine & Transmission). Description technique : After a long standstill the coolant and the intake air should both have settled close to ambient temperature. P011B compares the two sensors at start-up and is set when they disagree without either sensor showing a circuit fault. In the documented GM/Saab version the engine must have been off for more than 10 hours with no preheater detected; the fault counts if coolant reads at least 20 °C above intake air, or intake air at least 30 °C above coolant, and the coolant reading barely moves (2 °C or less) in the first 45 s. The code does not say which sensor is wrong – that has to be found by comparing both with the actual ambient temperature. Toyota resolved false settings on some 2015 V6 engines with new software. Ford and GM report the same idea under the individual sensor codes. Causes fréquentes : Coolant temperature sensor stuck or drifting [HIGH], Intake air temperature sensor drifting or heat-soaked [MEDIUM], Undetected preheater or uneven cooling [MEDIUM], Contact resistance at a sensor connector or ground [MEDIUM]. title: P011C: P011C - Charge Air Cooler Temperature/Intake Air Temperature Correlation Bank 1
content: CODE DÉFAUT OBD-II [P011C] : P011C - Charge Air Cooler Temperature/Intake Air Temperature Correlation Bank 1. Système : Powertrain (Engine & Transmission). Description technique : On turbocharged engines a charge air cooler temperature sensor sits downstream of the compressor, usually after the charge air cooler, and intake air temperature sensor 1 sits upstream near the air filter. While driving they differ by design, because compression heats the air. After a long standstill, however, both should read nearly the same, so the check runs at start-up. P011C is set when the two bank 1 sensors disagree there, without naming the faulty one. No manufacturer document using exactly this code was found; Ford performs the same comparison after 6 hours (tolerance about 17 °C on petrol, 16 °C on the 2023 diesel) but reports the outlier as P007B, P0111 or P00CE. Causes fréquentes : Charge air cooler temperature sensor drifting, oily or stuck [HIGH], Intake air temperature sensor 1 drifting [MEDIUM], Contact resistance at connector or shared ground [MEDIUM], Undetected preheating or uneven cooling (sun, residual heat) [LOW]. Urgence : High. Recommandation atelier : Estimated repair: 50€ - 300€ (0.3h - 1.5h labor). DIY feasible with standard tools.

title: P011D: P011D - Charge Air Cooler Temperature/Intake Air Temperature Correlation Bank 2
content: CODE DÉFAUT OBD-II [P011D] : P011D - Charge Air Cooler Temperature/Intake Air Temperature Correlation Bank 2. Système : Powertrain (Engine & Transmission). Description technique : This is the bank 2 counterpart of P011C and only exists on engines with two separate intake paths, each with its own charge air cooler temperature sensor and intake air temperature sensor – for example V engines with twin turbochargers and separate charge air coolers. After a long standstill both bank 2 sensors should read nearly the same; if they disagree at start-up, without either showing a circuit fault, P011D is set. The code does not identify which sensor is wrong. title: P0120: P0120 - Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor/Switch A Circuit
content: CODE DÉFAUT OBD-II [P0120] : P0120 - Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor/Switch A Circuit. Système : Powertrain (Engine & Transmission). Description technique : Sensor A is, in practice, throttle position sensor 1 at the throttle body; the accelerator pedal has its own codes (P2120 onwards). With a cable-operated throttle there is a single potentiometer (about 0.5 V closed to 4.5 V wide open). Electronic throttles have two sensors sharing a 5 V reference and ground, usually running in opposite directions – on GM throttle sensor 1 falls from 3–4 V at idle to below 1 V at full throttle. P0120 is the general circuit fault, used when the fault cannot be classed as low or high or when the sensor is digital. Ford sets it on digital SENT throttle sensors when the sensor reports an error for more than 4 s, together with the MIL and wrench lamp; Saab Trionic used it as a collective code. GM and Ford's analogue throttles report P0122/P0123 instead. Electronic throttles then fall back to a spring-loaded limp position with limited power. Causes fréquentes : Connector at the throttle body corroded or loose, broken wire [HIGH], Sensor or throttle body with integrated sensor faulty [MEDIUM], 5 V reference disturbed (short on another sensor of the same circuit) [MEDIUM], Engine control module faulty [LOW]. Urgence : Urgent / Danger. Recommandation atelier : Estimated repair: 30€ - 450€ (0.5h - 2h labor). DIY feasible with standard tools.

content: CODE DÉFAUT OBD-II [P0121] : P0121 - Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor/Switch A Circuit Range/Performance. Système : Powertrain (Engine & Transmission). Description technique : Sensor A is, in practice, throttle position sensor 1 at the throttle body; the accelerator pedal has its own codes (P2120 onwards). title: P0123: P0123 - Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor/Switch A Circuit High
content: CODE DÉFAUT OBD-II [P0123] : P0123 - Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor/Switch A Circuit High. Système : Powertrain (Engine & Transmission). Description technique : Sensor A is, in practice, throttle position sensor 1 at the throttle body; the accelerator pedal has its own codes (P2120 onwards). Electronic throttles have two sensors sharing a 5 V reference and ground, usually running in opposite directions – on GM throttle sensor 1 falls from 3–4 V at idle to below 1 V at full throttle. title: P0124: P0124 - Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor/Switch A Circuit Intermittent
content: CODE DÉFAUT OBD-II [P0124] : P0124 - Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor/Switch A Circuit Intermittent. Système : Powertrain (Engine & Transmission). title: P0125: P0125 - Insufficient Coolant Temperature for Closed Loop Fuel Control
content: CODE DÉFAUT OBD-II [P0125] : P0125 - Insufficient Coolant Temperature for Closed Loop Fuel Control. Système : Powertrain (Engine & Transmission). Description technique : Closed-loop mixture control using the oxygen sensors is only released once the coolant has reached a minimum temperature. CARB requires that this happens within set times – from 2006 two minutes if the engine starts up to 8 °C below the release temperature, five minutes if 8–19 °C below. P0125 means it took too long. Ford checks once per cold start and fails if coolant is still below 10 °C while its model already expects over 27 °C; Mitsubishi expects about 7 °C within 90–300 s and also fails if coolant drops back below 40 °C. Long idling suspends the test. Usual causes are a thermostat stuck open or a sensor reading too cold. GM does not use this code in the tables checked. Causes fréquentes : Thermostat stuck open (especially in cold weather) [HIGH], Coolant sensor reading too cold or slow (drift, contact resistance) [HIGH], Low coolant level or air at the sensor [MEDIUM], Much idling or coasting in frost [LOW]. Urgence : High. Recommandation atelier : Estimated repair: 40€ - 350€ (0.5h - 2.5h labor). DIY feasible with standard tools.

title: P0126: P0126 - Insufficient Coolant Temperature for Stable Operation
content: CODE DÉFAUT OBD-II [P0126] : P0126 - Insufficient Coolant Temperature for Stable Operation. Système : Powertrain (Engine & Transmission). Description technique : The generic title refers to a coolant temperature that is not reached for stable operation, i.e. for releasing further functions and diagnostics; how manufacturers implement it differs. The only implementation documented in a manufacturer source is Subaru's (via the Saab 9-2X service information): there P0126 is a stuck-sensor check – if the coolant signal changes by less than 5 mV during 20 s of driving or idling after start, the sensor counts as frozen. It runs once per drive cycle, lights the MIL after two consecutive cycles and has no fail-safe mode. Other interpretations, closer to a thermostat check, could not be verified in a manufacturer document. Causes fréquentes : Coolant sensor frozen or faulty (resistance does not change) [HIGH], Thermostat stuck open or low coolant [MEDIUM], Contact resistance in connector or wiring [LOW], Engine control module [LOW]. Urgence : High. Recommandation atelier : Estimated repair: 30€ - 300€ (0.3h - 2h labor). DIY feasible with standard tools.

title: P0127: P0127 - Intake Air Temperature Too High
content: CODE DÉFAUT OBD-II [P0127] : P0127 - Intake Air Temperature Too High. Système : Powertrain (Engine & Transmission). Description technique : P0127 is not a circuit fault but a functional check of the air path: the measured intake air temperature is too high for the operating state. The logic is documented for a Bosch EDC16 diesel (Saab 9-3): if the intake air exceeds 130 °C and does not fall below it within 45 s after the exhaust gas recirculation valve is closed, hot exhaust gas is evidently still entering or the sensor is wrong. The engine then disables EGR and runs in limp mode with reduced torque. GM has the code in its diesel software but disabled for US OBD II; Ford reports an overly hot intake air reading as P0111 instead. On other engines a hot reading can also come from warm under-bonnet air being drawn in. Causes fréquentes : EGR valve stuck open or not sealing (diesel) [HIGH], EGR cooler clogged or bypass flap stuck in bypass [MEDIUM], Charge air cooler dirty or airflow through it blocked [MEDIUM], Sensor reading wrong, or hot engine-bay air drawn in (loose intake duct) [MEDIUM]. Urgence : Urgent / Danger. Recommandation atelier : Estimated repair: 50€ - 1200€ (0.5h - 4h labor). Professional workshop recommended.

title: P0128: P0128 - Coolant Thermostat (Coolant Temperature Below Thermostat Regulating Temperature)
content: CODE DÉFAUT OBD-II [P0128] : P0128 - Coolant Thermostat (Coolant Temperature Below Thermostat Regulating Temperature). Système : Powertrain (Engine & Transmission). Description technique : After a cold start the thermostat stays closed so the engine warms up quickly. CARB requires the coolant to reach a temperature at most 11 °C below the thermostat's rated value within a set time. GM models the heat put in (fuel energy minus losses to ambient, cabin heater and coasting) and fails if enough energy has gone in without coolant reaching about 65 °C (55 °C in cold weather). Ford compares the measured value with a modelled one, typically failing below 78 °C with an 89 °C thermostat. The test runs once per drive cycle, pauses with much idling or below about −7 °C, and needs two trips. Usually the thermostat is stuck open; a sensor reading too low is the other suspect. Causes fréquentes : Thermostat stuck open or opening too early [HIGH], Coolant sensor reading too low, or corrosion and resistance in its circuit [MEDIUM], Low coolant level or air in the system [MEDIUM], Radiator fan running constantly (relay stuck, wrong control) [LOW]. Urgence : High. Recommandation atelier : Estimated repair: 60€ - 400€ (0.5h - 3h labor). DIY feasible with standard tools.

title: P0129: P0129 - Barometric Pressure Too Low
content: CODE DÉFAUT OBD-II [P0129] : P0129 - Barometric Pressure Too Low. Système : Powertrain (Engine & Transmission). Description technique : The engine control module needs the ambient air pressure for mixture, altitude correction and boost limits. It comes either from a dedicated barometric sensor or from the MAP sensor, read at key-on with the engine stopped and updated at wide-open throttle. P0129 means this value is lower than physically possible – even on the highest drivable passes air pressure stays around 50 kPa, and GM and Ford use 50 kPa as their lower plausibility limit. Usual causes are a MAP or baro sensor reading too low, a blocked sensor port or high resistance in the wiring. No manufacturer document naming exactly this code was found: GM and Ford file the same finding under P2227. Causes fréquentes : MAP or baro sensor reading too low (dirty, oiled, drifted) [HIGH], High resistance or corrosion in signal wire or connector [MEDIUM], Sensor port or hose blocked [MEDIUM], Control module (baro sensor often built in) or software [LOW]. title: P012A: P012A - Turbocharger/Supercharger Inlet Pressure Sensor A Circuit
content: CODE DÉFAUT OBD-II [P012A] : P012A - Turbocharger/Supercharger Inlet Pressure Sensor A Circuit. Système : Powertrain (Engine & Transmission). Description technique : The turbocharger/supercharger inlet pressure sensor A sits between the air filter and the compressor. The engine uses it for the compressor pressure ratio, to judge air filter restriction (ambient minus inlet pressure) and to cross-check the other pressure sensors. P012A is the general circuit fault. Ford's 2023 diesels use a digital SENT sensor here and set P012A when its error flag is raised or the value exceeds a limit for 5 s; lost communication is reported separately (U068B). FCA's 2019 Jeep Wrangler 2.0 turbo could set P012A, P012C and P012D falsely and was fixed with new engine software, so the software level is worth checking before replacing parts. GM's supercharged V8 uses only P012B–P012D. A substitute value, usually ambient pressure, is used. Causes fréquentes : Connector or wiring open, corroded or shorted [HIGH], Sensor faulty (SENT sensor reports internal error) [MEDIUM], Control module software (false setting) [MEDIUM], Engine control module faulty [LOW]. Urgence : Urgent / Danger. Recommandation atelier : Estimated repair: 20€ - 250€ (0.3h - 1h labor). DIY feasible with standard tools.

title: P012F: P012F - Engine Coolant Temperature / Engine Oil Temperature Correlation
content: CODE DÉFAUT OBD-II [P012F] : P012F - Engine Coolant Temperature / Engine Oil Temperature Correlation. Système : Powertrain (Engine & Transmission). Description technique : P012F compares the coolant temperature sensor with the engine oil temperature sensor. The documented user is Ford's Power Stroke diesel. After a calibration update for the 6.0 litre engine, Ford uses it to monitor oil cooler efficiency: if the oil gets much hotter than the coolant at certain speed and load, the oil-to-coolant heat exchanger is probably clogged, and P012F sets together with the wrench lamp. On the 6.7 litre (2015–2018) several bulletins treat P012F as a false setting – partly below 5 °C ambient – cured by reprogramming the engine module. Ford's 2023 diesels run the cold-start comparison of coolant against oil temperature (35 °C limit after 6 h) under P0196 instead. GM does not use the code, and the code does not say which sensor or which system is at fault. Causes fréquentes : Oil cooler (oil-to-coolant heat exchanger) clogged – oil much hotter than coolant [HIGH], Engine module software (false setting, especially in cold weather) [MEDIUM], Coolant or oil temperature sensor inaccurate, or its wiring faulty [MEDIUM], Thermostat stuck open or low coolant [LOW]. title: P0130: P0130 - O2 Sensor Circuit Bank 1 Sensor 1
content: CODE DÉFAUT OBD-II [P0130] : P0130 - O2 Sensor Circuit Bank 1 Sensor 1. Système : Powertrain (Engine & Transmission). Description technique : The oxygen sensor before the catalytic converter on bank 1 (sensor 1) is the main control sensor for the mixture. It is either a switching sensor (about 0.1 V lean to 0.9 V rich) or a wide-band sensor that works with a pump current evaluated by an interface chip. P0130 is the general circuit code, and manufacturers fill it very differently. Ford used it up to 2010 as the collective code for all wiring faults reported by the wide-band interface chip and has split it into specific codes since 2011. Subaru sets it when the interface voltages leave their range for 5 s, with immediate MIL. GM calls it 'closed loop performance': cross-talk from the heater (signal rises above 2 V with the heater off) or disagreement with the downstream sensor, two trips. A stored code usually switches mixture control to open loop and suspends adaptation and converter monitoring. Causes fréquentes : Wiring or connector of the bank 1 upstream sensor damaged, corroded or wet [HIGH], Oxygen sensor faulty internally [HIGH], Exhaust leak ahead of the sensor or mixture fault (plausibility versions) [MEDIUM], Wrong or aftermarket sensor type [LOW]. Urgence : High. Recommandation atelier : Estimated repair: 60€ - 350€ (0.5h - 2h labor). DIY feasible with standard tools.

title: P0131: P0131 - O2 Sensor Circuit Low Voltage Bank 1 Sensor 1
content: CODE DÉFAUT OBD-II [P0131] : P0131 - O2 Sensor Circuit Low Voltage Bank 1 Sensor 1. Système : Powertrain (Engine & Transmission). Description technique : The oxygen sensor before the catalytic converter on bank 1 (sensor 1) is the main control sensor for the mixture. It is either a switching sensor (about 0.1 V lean to 0.9 V rich) or a wide-band sensor that works with a pump current evaluated by an interface chip. On switching sensors it means the signal stays below about 40–60 mV (GM, two trips; some GM engines also require the downstream sensor to read rich at the same time, since a genuinely lean mixture would show there too). On wide-band sensors (Ford from 2011, GM) it has nothing to do with the mixture: the interface chip reports one of the sensor wires shorted to ground. A really lean mixture leads to P0171/P2195 rather than this code. A stored code usually switches mixture control to open loop and suspends adaptation and converter monitoring. Causes fréquentes : Signal wire (or a wide-band sensor wire) shorted to ground, e.g. chafed on exhaust or gearbox [HIGH], Sensor faulty or poisoned (permanently lean signal) [HIGH], Large exhaust leak ahead of the sensor or misfires [MEDIUM], Connector wet or corroded [MEDIUM]. title: P0132: P0132 - O2 Sensor Circuit High Voltage Bank 1 Sensor 1
content: CODE DÉFAUT OBD-II [P0132] : P0132 - O2 Sensor Circuit High Voltage Bank 1 Sensor 1. Système : Powertrain (Engine & Transmission). Description technique : The oxygen sensor before the catalytic converter on bank 1 (sensor 1) is the main control sensor for the mixture. It is either a switching sensor (about 0.1 V lean to 0.9 V rich) or a wide-band sensor that works with a pump current evaluated by an interface chip. On switching sensors the signal is above what the sensor can physically produce (about 1 V): Ford above 1.1 V for 10 s, GM above 1050 mV, Saab Trionic above 1.5 V for 5 s. The cause is almost always electrical – the heater supply or battery voltage on the signal wire, or a heater-to-signal short inside the sensor; some GM modules also read an open wire this way. On wide-band sensors the interface chip reports a sensor wire shorted to voltage. If P0132 and P0138 appear together, a shared short in the harness is likely. A stored code usually switches mixture control to open loop and suspends adaptation and converter monitoring. Causes fréquentes : Signal wire shorted to the heater supply or battery voltage (melted or chafed harness) [HIGH], Sensor faulty internally (heater-to-signal short) [HIGH], Open or high-resistance signal or ground wire (GM reads its bias voltage) [MEDIUM], Moisture or corrosion in the connector [MEDIUM].
