title: P0134: P0134 - O2 Sensor Circuit No Activity Detected Bank 1 Sensor 1
content: CODE DÉFAUT OBD-II [P0134] : P0134 - O2 Sensor Circuit No Activity Detected Bank 1 Sensor 1. Système : Powertrain (Engine & Transmission). Description technique : The oxygen sensor before the catalytic converter on bank 1 (sensor 1) is the main control sensor for the mixture. It is either a switching sensor (about 0.1 V lean to 0.9 V rich) or a wide-band sensor that works with a pump current evaluated by an interface chip. P0134 means the sensor delivers no moving signal, typically because the circuit is open or the cell is cold or dead. The control module feeds a bias voltage, and that is all it sees: GM fails a signal stuck at 350–550 mV (or above 1700 mV with a 1.9 V bias) after warm-up, within about 15 s, or a cell resistance above 20 kΩ in hot exhaust; two trips. Subaru's wide-band sensor fails above 500 Ω cell impedance with immediate MIL. Ford's Bosch wide-band systems have used P2237 for this since 2011. A stored code usually switches mixture control to open loop and suspends adaptation and converter monitoring. Causes fréquentes : Open or high-resistance signal or ground wire, connector loose or corroded [HIGH], Sensor faulty (cell high-resistance, worn out) [HIGH], Sensor heater faulty – sensor does not get hot enough [MEDIUM], Exhaust leak ahead of the sensor or cracked sensor [LOW]. title: P0135: P0135 - O2 Sensor Heater Circuit Bank 1 Sensor 1
content: CODE DÉFAUT OBD-II [P0135] : P0135 - O2 Sensor Heater Circuit Bank 1 Sensor 1. Système : Powertrain (Engine & Transmission). Description technique : The upstream oxygen sensor on bank 1 (sensor 1) has an electric heater so that it reaches its working temperature of about 300 °C soon after a cold start. The control module switches the heater on the ground side and checks driver voltage and heater current: GM fails it outside 0.3–2.5 A (or 3.1 A) and calls it 'heater performance', Ford outside roughly 0.22–0.465 A minimum to 3 A, Saab Trionic outside 0.5–2.3 A for 5 s. Manufacturers split heater faults differently between P0030–P0032, P0053 and P0135. With the heater dead, closed-loop control starts late after a cold start. If P0135 and P0141 appear together, check the shared fuse. Causes fréquentes : Heater element of the sensor burnt out (sensor must be replaced) [HIGH], Fuse or relay of the heater supply faulty [MEDIUM], Heater wiring or connector open, corroded or shorted [MEDIUM], Unsuitable replacement sensor (different heater resistance) [LOW]. title: P0136: P0136 - O2 Sensor Circuit Bank 1 Sensor 2
content: CODE DÉFAUT OBD-II [P0136] : P0136 - O2 Sensor Circuit Bank 1 Sensor 2. Système : Powertrain (Engine & Transmission). Description technique : The oxygen sensor after the catalytic converter on bank 1 (sensor 2) is a switching sensor (about 0.1–0.9 V) used for converter monitoring and fine mixture trim. P0136 is the general circuit code, and its exact meaning varies by manufacturer. Ford sets it as 'no activity' in a functional check: if the sensor never swings beyond about 0.42/0.48 V despite rich and lean phases – if needed after forced enrichment and leaning – once per drive cycle. Opel/GM Europe set it if the average voltage stays outside 400–500 mV after 10 min of closed loop; older Bosch Motronic if it stays at 0 V for 200 s despite heating. GM North America does not use P0136. When it fails, the control module stops the downstream trim and cannot evaluate the converter; there is no limp mode. Causes fréquentes : Downstream sensor aged or poisoned (stays in the middle band) [HIGH], Signal or ground wire open or high-resistance, connector corroded [MEDIUM], Sensor heater failed (sensor stays cold) [MEDIUM], Exhaust leak ahead of the sensor [LOW]. title: P0137: P0137 - O2 Sensor Circuit Low Voltage Bank 1 Sensor 2
content: CODE DÉFAUT OBD-II [P0137] : P0137 - O2 Sensor Circuit Low Voltage Bank 1 Sensor 2. Système : Powertrain (Engine & Transmission). Description technique : The oxygen sensor after the catalytic converter on bank 1 (sensor 2) is a switching sensor (about 0.1–0.9 V) used for converter monitoring and fine mixture trim. Documented limits: GM below 40–60 mV (two trips); Ford switches in a pull-up and reads open above 1 MΩ (20 kΩ from 2020) or short to ground below 10 Ω, within 10 s. When it fails, the control module stops the downstream trim and cannot evaluate the converter; there is no limp mode. title: P0138: P0138 - O2 Sensor Circuit High Voltage Bank 1 Sensor 2
content: CODE DÉFAUT OBD-II [P0138] : P0138 - O2 Sensor Circuit High Voltage Bank 1 Sensor 2. Système : Powertrain (Engine & Transmission). Description technique : The oxygen sensor after the catalytic converter on bank 1 (sensor 2) is a switching sensor (about 0.1–0.9 V) used for converter monitoring and fine mixture trim. Monitored continuously, two trips. When it fails, the control module stops the downstream trim and cannot evaluate the converter; there is no limp mode. title: P0139: P0139 - O2 Sensor Circuit Slow Response Bank 1 Sensor 2
content: CODE DÉFAUT OBD-II [P0139] : P0139 - O2 Sensor Circuit Slow Response Bank 1 Sensor 2. Système : Powertrain (Engine & Transmission). Description technique : The oxygen sensor after the catalytic converter on bank 1 (sensor 2) is a switching sensor (about 0.1–0.9 V) used for converter monitoring and fine mixture trim. P0139 means the sensor reacts too slowly to mixture changes. Subaru measures it around fuel cut-off: rich to lean from 500 to 300 mV must take no more than 0.51 s, lean to rich from 300 to 500 mV no more than 2 s; two drive cycles set the MIL. CARB requires such a test because a sluggish downstream sensor could let a worn converter pass. Since about 2009–2011 GM and Ford report this as direction-specific codes P013A–P013F instead; P0139 remains in use on older, Asian and Jaguar Land Rover systems. When it fails, the control module stops the downstream trim and cannot evaluate the converter; there is no limp mode. Causes fréquentes : Sensor aged or contaminated (oil ash, silicone, additives) [HIGH], Exhaust leak ahead of the sensor [MEDIUM], Sensor heater weak, sensor too cold [MEDIUM], High-resistance ground or connector [LOW]. title: P013A: P013A - O2 Sensor Slow Response - Rich to Lean Bank 1 Sensor 2
content: CODE DÉFAUT OBD-II [P013A] : P013A - O2 Sensor Slow Response - Rich to Lean Bank 1 Sensor 2. Système : Powertrain (Engine & Transmission). Description technique : The downstream oxygen sensor (sensor 2, after the catalytic converter) is used for fine mixture trim and to monitor the converter. 'Slow response' means the signal transition itself is too sluggish – it takes too long to pass between two voltage levels. This code covers the rich-to-lean direction, usually tested during deceleration fuel cut-off. GM forces the test itself and measures how quickly the signal passes from 450 to 150 mV relative to air flow; a filtered value above its limit sets the code after one trip (fallback: target not reached before about 60 g of air). Ford measures the slew rate during fuel cut-off, normalised to the converter's stored oxygen. Lexus traced one case to a leaking manifold gasket ahead of the sensor; on Ram diesels it is soot-related. CARB requires separate detection of slow and delayed faults in each direction (phased in from 2009 for downstream and 2011 for upstream sensors). Causes fréquentes : Downstream oxygen sensor aged or contaminated (soot, oil, silicone, coolant) [HIGH], Exhaust leak between manifold/turbo and the sensor [MEDIUM], Converter faulty or non-original with different oxygen storage [LOW], Control module software too sensitive (update available) [LOW]. Urgence : High. Recommandation atelier : Estimated repair: 60€ - 250€ (0.5h - 1.5h labor). DIY feasible with standard tools.

Description technique : The downstream oxygen sensor on bank 1 (sensor 2) has an electric heater so it reaches its working temperature quickly. GM fails it outside 0.3–2.5 A (two trips; pure circuit faults are P0036–P0038 there); Ford uses P0141 as its general heater circuit code with a current window of roughly 0.22–0.465 A minimum to 3 A maximum depending on sensor supplier. content: CODE DÉFAUT OBD-II [P0142] : P0142 - O2 Sensor Circuit Bank 1 Sensor 3. Système : Powertrain (Engine & Transmission). Description technique : Sensor 3 is a third oxygen sensor on bank 1, behind a second converter or converter brick. It only exists on some vehicles – documented for Jaguar Land Rover's 3.0 V6 supercharged (2013–2016, where sensor 2 is 'mid-cat' and sensor 3 'post-cat') and Ford systems that monitor part of the converter volume. title: P0148: P0148 - Fuel Delivery Error
content: CODE DÉFAUT OBD-II [P0148] : P0148 - Fuel Delivery Error. Système : Powertrain (Engine & Transmission). Description technique : P0148 is an early, rather unspecific OBD II code: the control module finds that the fuel delivered does not match what was requested. Saab's 3.0 V6 diesel (Isuzu) uses it for leak detection: from the balance of quantity and rail pressure it recognises a leak of 90 mm³ per crankshaft revolution, monitored continuously up to 6,400 rpm, and then shuts the engine off – a restart is only possible in the next drive cycle. Ford lists P0148 in the fuel monitor of its 2020–2023 petrol engines, alongside P0171/P0172, without describing the logic. Newer systems usually report such faults more precisely as P0087/P0088 (rail pressure) or P0093 (large leak). Causes fréquentes : Fuel leak in the high-pressure or return section (line, rail, injector leakage) [HIGH], Fuel filter clogged or lift pump weak [MEDIUM], High-pressure or injection pump worn [MEDIUM], Pressure or volume control valve faulty [LOW]. Urgence : Urgent / Danger. Recommandation atelier : Estimated repair: 50€ - 2500€ (0.5h - 6h labor). Professional workshop recommended.

title: P0149: P0149 - Fuel Timing Error
content: CODE DÉFAUT OBD-II [P0149] : P0149 - Fuel Timing Error. Système : Powertrain (Engine & Transmission). Description technique : P0149 is a diesel code for a deviation of the actual from the target start of injection. On distributor pumps such as the Bosch VP44, a timing device sets the delivery start, and the pump control unit compares the actual position with the target. On the 2003 Saab 9-3 2.2 TiD (GM/Opel engine) P0149 means injection too early – too late is the manufacturer code P1149; it is monitored continuously above 600 rpm and leads to limp mode with limited fuel quantity. CARB has required injection timing monitoring for all diesels since model year 2010. On common-rail systems timing is mostly covered by injector-related codes, so P0149 is rare there. Causes fréquentes : Injection pump wrongly set or drive (belt, key) shifted [HIGH], Timing device or timing solenoid of the pump faulty [MEDIUM], Air in the fuel or low supply pressure [MEDIUM], Pump control unit faulty [LOW]. Urgence : Urgent / Danger. Recommandation atelier : Estimated repair: 100€ - 3000€ (1h - 8h labor). Professional workshop recommended.

title: P014A: P014A - O2 Sensor Delayed Response - Rich to Lean Bank 2 Sensor 2
content: CODE DÉFAUT OBD-II [P014A] : P014A - O2 Sensor Delayed Response - Rich to Lean Bank 2 Sensor 2. Système : Powertrain (Engine & Transmission). Description technique : The downstream oxygen sensor (sensor 2, after the catalytic converter) is used for fine mixture trim and to monitor the converter. 'Delayed response' means the sensor starts reacting too late, or does not reach the target level at all, after the mixture has changed. This code covers the rich-to-lean direction, usually tested during deceleration fuel cut-off. Bank 2 only exists on V and boxer engines. GM checks whether the signal falls below 450 mV before about 45 g of air have passed after the forced change; failing needs two trips. Ford uses the same stuck-in-range test for bank 2, failing after three bad results in a row. CARB requires separate detection of slow and delayed faults in each direction (phased in from 2009 for downstream and 2011 for upstream sensors). Causes fréquentes : Downstream oxygen sensor aged or contaminated (soot, oil, silicone, coolant) [HIGH], Exhaust leak between manifold/turbo and the sensor [MEDIUM], Converter faulty or non-original with different oxygen storage [MEDIUM], Control module software too sensitive (update available) [LOW]. Urgence : High. Recommandation atelier : Estimated repair: 60€ - 250€ (0.5h - 1.5h labor). DIY feasible with standard tools.

title: P0150: P0150 - O2 Sensor Circuit Bank 2 Sensor 1
content: CODE DÉFAUT OBD-II [P0150] : P0150 - O2 Sensor Circuit Bank 2 Sensor 1. Système : Powertrain (Engine & Transmission). Description technique : The oxygen sensor before the catalytic converter on bank 2 (sensor 1) is the main control sensor for the mixture. It is either a switching sensor (about 0.1 V lean to 0.9 V rich) or a wide-band sensor that works with a pump current evaluated by an interface chip. Bank 2 exists only on engines with two exhaust manifolds. P0150 is the bank 2 counterpart of P0130. Ford used it up to 2010 as the collective code for wiring faults of the bank 2 wide-band sensor reported by the interface chip and has used specific codes since 2011 (P0151, P0152, P2240/P2247/P2254). Other makers fill it as for bank 1 – an interface voltage check, a collective code or a plausibility test. No bank 2-specific manufacturer thresholds were found. If P0130 and P0150 appear together, look for a shared cause such as supply, ground or the control module. A stored code usually switches mixture control to open loop and suspends adaptation and converter monitoring. Causes fréquentes : Wiring or connector of the bank 2 upstream sensor damaged, corroded or wet [HIGH], Oxygen sensor faulty internally [HIGH], Exhaust leak ahead of the sensor or mixture fault (plausibility versions) [MEDIUM], Control module or sensor interface chip faulty [LOW]. Urgence : High. Recommandation atelier : Estimated repair: 60€ - 350€ (0.5h - 2.5h labor). DIY feasible with standard tools.
